rows.steps:
Confirm the hang before the first cut||Wine rack. Wall-mounted wine rack 24" wide × 12" deep × 14 1/4" high. Holds 12 bottles — 3 rows × 4 across, one opening per bottle (rows on a 4 1/2" pitch, one bottle high). Built 14 1/4" tall — just the rows the bottles need. This hangs on the wall, so the layout marks go on the wall. Find two studs. Typical bottom sits about 36–42" off the floor, or sit it on a counter and still screw it into the studs with 3" structural screws so it stays upright. 13 parts on this list. Assumed 24" wide (default size) — type a width to lock it. Assumed 14 1/4" tall (default size) — type a height to lock it.||This is a wine rack, not a bookcase. Bottles lie on their sides. If a number disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). 1 Left upright 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". 2 shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 3 Bottle rails 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". 2 Grid shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 3 Dividers 12 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". 1 A Back 22 1/2 × 14 1/4 × 3/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Stand the rack||E Left upright — 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4"; E Right upright — 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". A Back — 22 1/2 × 14 1/4 × 3/4". D Shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; D Shelf 4 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into every shelf at those marked heights. Then screw the bottom shelf and the shelf above the bottle rows into the divider ends, and the A back onto the shelf edges. Use fixed shelves here, screwed in place — a row of bottles is heavy. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Lay the Left upright flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the next parts fasten to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: Tops of the D shelves sit 3/4" and 14 1/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 13 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both E uprights before you set any shelf. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Tops of the C grid shelves sit 5 1/4" and 9 3/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 4 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both E uprights before you set any grid shelf. Or cut a spacer block 4 1/2" long, stand it on the bottom edge, and rest the lowest grid shelf on it. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Drive 18 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Every opening should take a bottle with room to spare.
Notch and slot the bottle grid||. C Grid shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; C Grid shelf 2 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Dividers: cut 2 notches 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the front edge, one where each shelf crosses, at 3 3/4" and 8 1/4" up from the bottom end. Middle shelves: cut 3 notches 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the back edge, one at each divider crossing, at 5 1/16", 10 7/8" and 16 11/16" from the left end. Saw both sides of each notch and chisel out the waste. Slot every divider down over the middle shelves so the front edges line up — an egg-crate grid. Dry-fit, then glue the laps. Fasten the C Grid shelf 1 to both E uprights with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Cut one notch, test it on a scrap of the same board, then cut the rest. A snug hand-press fit is right — no hammering.
Glue the bottle rails||B Bottle rail 1 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; B Bottle rail 2 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; B Bottle rail 3 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". Glue a 1 1/2" rail on the front of every shelf that carries a row of bottles so they stay on. #8 × 1 1/4" screws from behind the rail into the shelf front edge. Drive 21 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||The rail stands on the front edge of the shelf. Wipe squeeze-out before it skins. Bottles lie on their sides, necks facing out.
Set the Bottle divider 1, Bottle divider 2 and Bottle divider 3||Set the Bottle divider 1 on the Shelf 1 and the B Bottle rail 1. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Set the Bottle divider 2 on the Shelf 1 and the B Bottle rail 1. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Set the Bottle divider 3 on the Shelf 1 and the B Bottle rail 1. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Center F Bottle divider 1: 5 1/16" from the inside face of E Left upright and 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 2. Square a pencil line across D Shelf 1 at each mark and stand the divider on it. Center F Bottle divider 2: 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 1 and 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 3. Center F Bottle divider 3: 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 2 and 5 1/16" from the inside face of E Right upright. Drive 48 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 101 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||It goes on once every part under it is in place.
Hang it on studs||Find two studs. Predrill the A back. Drive 3" structural screws through the A back into the studs — 4 to 6 screws. A loaded wine rack will rip off drywall anchors.||Guidance only — hit a stud. Confirm the hang height so you can reach a bottle.

Confirm the footprint before the first cut||Shoe rack 32" wide. Unit 32" wide × 12" deep × 16 1/4" high. Freestanding rectangle. Mark the footprint on the floor. Check it is square. 8 parts on this list. Assumed 16 1/4" tall (shoe rack class default) — type a height to lock it. Assumed 12" deep (shoe rack class default) — type a depth to lock it.||If a number on this plan disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list. Geometry is from the bench, not from the prompt's adjectives.
Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8 and 1/4" plywood (backer)||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). From the 3/4" Plywood 4×8: 1 Left upright 16 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 16 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". 1 B Bottom 30 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". 1 C Shoe shelf 30 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". 1 D Top 30 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". 2 Cubby dividers 14 3/4 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". From the 1/4" plywood (backer): 1 A Back 30 1/2 × 16 1/4 × 1/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Stand the main box||Lay the two E uprights on edge. E Left upright — 16 1/4 × 12 × 3/4"; E Right upright — 16 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". One join: attach B Bottom to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Where: Top of B Bottom sits 3/4" up from the floor — flush with the bottom ends of both E uprights. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. In all, this step drives 22 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws, from the model's joints.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Attach D Top to both E uprights||One join: attach D Top to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Where: Top of D Top sits 16 1/4" up from the floor — flush with the top ends of both E uprights. Its underside rests on the top of both F cubby dividers, 15 1/2" up from the floor. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. These screws are counted in another step's total.||One join at a time — dry-fit, then glue and drive the screws for this join only.
Set cubby dividers||F Cubby divider 1 — 14 3/4 × 11 3/4 × 3/4"; F Cubby divider 2 — 14 3/4 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". Space them evenly. Screw through the D top, bottom, and back into each divider. Where: F Cubby divider 1 stands 9 9/16" from the inside face of E Left upright and 9 15/16" from F Cubby divider 2. Square a pencil line across B Bottom at each mark and stand the divider on it. F Cubby divider 2 stands 9 15/16" from F Cubby divider 1 and 9 9/16" from the inside face of E Right upright. Drive 12 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||
Attach A Back to the back of the box||One join: attach A Back to the back edges of both E Uprights, B Bottom and D Top and both F Cubby dividers with 18 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws, one about every 8" along each edge. Square the box first: both diagonals measure the same. Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. These screws are counted in another step's total.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Glue 1 fixed shelf||C Shoe shelf — 30 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into each shelf at those marked heights. Square every bay. The back is already on and square: slide each shelf in to touch it, then drive 4 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws through A Back into the shelf back edges, one about every 8". These shelves are fixed — no pins. Where: Top of C Shoe shelf sits 7 3/4" up from the top of B Bottom (8 1/2" from the floor). Mark 7 3/4" up from the top of B Bottom on the inside face of both E uprights and line the top face up with the marks. Or cut a spacer block 7" long, stand it on B Bottom, and rest the part on it while you fasten it. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Drive 12 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 46 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Wipe squeeze-out.
Level it||Level the unit. The A back is already on it so the box stays square. If it sits on a floor that is out, shim the feet, keeping the main box square.||Guidance only — confirm the real footprint before you cut. Not stamped engineering.

Lay out the footprint on the bench||Tape a rectangle 36" × 12" on the bench. Mark centerlines both ways. The faces go up from this outline.||A square base keeps every later part true.
Cut every marked length||PVC cutter or a fine hacksaw. Deburr so each end seats in the fitting. The cut list is the full list — same letter is the same cut. 58 pieces: 8 × 12", 16 × 11 1/4", 6 × 11", 16 × 8 3/8", 4 × 3 7/8", 8 × 3 5/8".||A ragged end will not bottom out in a slip tee.
Stand the sides — 16 pieces||16 pieces: 16 × 8 3/8". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs.||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Run the rails — 42 pieces||42 pieces: 8 × 12", 16 × 11 1/4", 6 × 11", 4 × 3 7/8", 8 × 3 5/8". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs.||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Check plumb and square||Stand it up. Sight the long edges. If a face racks, find the soft joint and re-join it.||A lean now is a lean forever.

rows.cuts: 1|33|18|0.25|Back||1/4" plywood 4x8 (backer);1|33|11.75|1.5|Bottom||2×2 (8 ft);1|33|11.75|1.5|Shoe shelf|Egg-crate half-lap: cut 2 notches 1 1/2" wide × 5 7/8" deep from the back edge, one at each divider crossing, at 9 3/4" and 21 3/4" from the left end.|2×2 (8 ft);1|33|11.75|1.5|Top||2×2 (8 ft);2|18|12|1.5|Upright||2×2 (8 ft);2|15|11.75|1.5|Cubby divider|Egg-crate half-lap: cut a notch 1 1/2" wide × 5 7/8" deep from the front edge, one where each shelf crosses, at 6 3/8" up from the bottom end.|2×2 (8 ft)
rows.steps:
Confirm the footprint before the first cut||Shoe rack. Unit 36" wide × 12" deep × 18" high. Freestanding rectangle. Mark the footprint on the floor. Check it is square. 8 parts on this list. Assumed 36" wide (shoe rack class default) — type a width to lock it. Assumed 18" tall (shoe rack class default) — type a height to lock it. Assumed 12" deep (shoe rack class default) — type a depth to lock it.||If a number on this plan disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list. Geometry is from the bench, not from the prompt's adjectives.
Cut the 2×2 (8 ft) and 1/4" plywood (backer)||Hand saw or circular saw. Square every cut. Predrill near the ends — boards split. From the 2×2 (8 ft): 1 Left upright 18 × 12 × 1 1/2". 1 Right upright 18 × 12 × 1 1/2". 1 B Bottom 33 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". 1 C Shoe shelf 33 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". 1 D Top 33 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". 2 Cubby dividers 15 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". From the 1/4" plywood (backer): 1 A Back 33 × 18 × 1/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Board ends split. Predrill.
Stand the main box||Lay the two E uprights on edge. E Left upright — 18 × 12 × 1 1/2"; E Right upright — 18 × 12 × 1 1/2". One join: attach B Bottom to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the wood does not split. Where: Top of B Bottom sits 1 1/2" up from the floor — flush with the bottom ends of both E uprights. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. In all, this step drives 24 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws, from the model's joints.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Attach D Top to both E uprights||One join: attach D Top to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the wood does not split. Where: Top of D Top sits 18" up from the floor — flush with the top ends of both E uprights. Its underside rests on the top of both F cubby dividers, 16 1/2" up from the floor. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. These screws are counted in another step's total.||One join at a time — dry-fit, then glue and drive the screws for this join only.
Set cubby dividers||F Cubby divider 1 — 15 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2"; F Cubby divider 2 — 15 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". Space them evenly. Screw through the D top, bottom, and back into each divider. Where: F Cubby divider 1 stands 9 3/4" from the inside face of E Left upright and 10 1/2" from F Cubby divider 2. Square a pencil line across B Bottom at each mark and stand the divider on it. F Cubby divider 2 stands 10 1/2" from F Cubby divider 1 and 9 3/4" from the inside face of E Right upright. Drive 12 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||
Attach A Back to the back of the box||One join: attach A Back to the back edges of both E Uprights, B Bottom and D Top and both F Cubby dividers with 20 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws, one about every 8" along each edge. Square the box first: both diagonals measure the same. Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the wood does not split. These screws are counted in another step's total.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Glue 1 fixed shelf||C Shoe shelf — 33 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". Glue and #8 × 2 1/2" screws through the uprights into each shelf at those marked heights. Square every bay. The back is already on and square: slide each shelf in to touch it, then drive 5 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws through A Back into the shelf back edges, one about every 8". These shelves are fixed — no pins. Where: Top of C Shoe shelf sits 7 7/8" up from the top of B Bottom (9 3/8" from the floor). Mark 7 7/8" up from the top of B Bottom on the inside face of both E uprights and line the top face up with the marks. Or cut a spacer block 6 3/8" long, stand it on B Bottom, and rest the part on it while you fasten it. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Drive 9 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 45 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||Predrill near the ends so the wood does not split. Wipe squeeze-out.
Level it||Level the unit. The A back is already on it so the box stays square. If it sits on a floor that is out, shim the feet, keeping the main box square.||Guidance only — confirm the real footprint before you cut. Not stamped engineering.

rows.steps:
Confirm the footprint before the first cut||Magazine rack. Unit 16" wide × 10" deep × 24" high. Freestanding rectangle. Mark the footprint on the floor. Check it is square. 7 parts on this list. Assumed 16" wide (default size) — type a width to lock it. Assumed 24" tall (default size) — type a height to lock it. Assumed 10" deep (default size) — type a depth to lock it.||If a number on this plan disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list. Geometry is from the bench, not from the prompt's adjectives.
Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). 1 Left upright 24 × 10 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 24 × 10 × 3/4". 1 D Bottom 14 1/2 × 9 1/4 × 3/4". 1 E Top 14 1/2 × 9 1/4 × 3/4". 1 A Back 24 × 14 1/2 × 3/4". 2 Dividers 22 1/2 × 9 1/4 × 3/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Stand the main box||Lay the two B uprights on edge. B Left upright — 24 × 10 × 3/4"; B Right upright — 24 × 10 × 3/4". One join: attach A Back to both B uprights with 6 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws (3 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. In all, this step drives 18 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws, from the model's joints.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Attach D Bottom to both B uprights||One join: attach D Bottom to both B uprights with 4 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Where: Top of D Bottom sits 3/4" up from the floor — flush with the bottom ends of both B uprights. Front edge flush with the front of both B uprights. These screws are counted in another step's total.||One join at a time — dry-fit, then glue and drive the screws for this join only.
Attach E Top to both B uprights||One join: attach E Top to both B uprights with 4 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Where: Top of E Top sits 24" up from the floor — flush with the top ends of both B uprights. Its underside rests on the top of both C dividers, 23 1/4" up from the floor. Front edge flush with the front of both B uprights. These screws are counted in another step's total.||One join at a time — dry-fit, then glue and drive the screws for this join only.
Set remaining dividers||Slot 1 — 22 1/2 × 9 1/4 × 3/4"; Slot 2 — 22 1/2 × 9 1/4 × 3/4". Plumb each one. Screw through the A back and the nearest shelf or top. Set the Slot 1 on the D Bottom. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Center C Slot 1: 4 5/16" from the inside face of B Left upright and 4 5/16" from C Slot 2. Square a pencil line across D Bottom at each mark and stand the divider on it. Center C Slot 2: 4 5/16" from C Slot 1 and 4 5/16" from the inside face of B Right upright. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 32 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||
Level it||Level the unit. The A back is already on it so the box stays square. If it sits on a floor that is out, shim the feet, keeping the main box square.||Guidance only — confirm the real footprint before you cut. Not stamped engineering.

This hangs on the wall, so the layout marks go on the wall. Find two studs. Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). 1 Left upright 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". 2 shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 3 Bottle rails 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". 2 Grid shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 3 Dividers 12 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". 1 A Back 22 1/2 × 14 1/4 × 3/4". Stand the rack||E Left upright — 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4"; E Right upright — 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". A Back — 22 1/2 × 14 1/4 × 3/4". D Shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; D Shelf 4 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into every shelf at those marked heights. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Lay the Left upright flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the next parts fasten to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: Tops of the D shelves sit 3/4" and 14 1/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 13 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both E uprights before you set any shelf. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Tops of the C grid shelves sit 5 1/4" and 9 3/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 4 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both E uprights before you set any grid shelf. Or cut a spacer block 4 1/2" long, stand it on the bottom edge, and rest the lowest grid shelf on it. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Drive 18 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Cut one notch, test it on a scrap of the same board, then cut the rest. Glue a 1 1/2" rail on the front of every shelf that carries a row of bottles so they stay on. #8 × 1 1/4" screws from behind the rail into the shelf front edge. Drive 21 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||The rail stands on the front edge of the shelf. Wipe squeeze-out before it skins. Bottles lie on their sides, necks facing out.
Set the Bottle divider 1, Bottle divider 2 and Bottle divider 3||Set the Bottle divider 1 on the Shelf 1 and the B Bottle rail 1. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Set the Bottle divider 2 on the Shelf 1 and the B Bottle rail 1. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Set the Bottle divider 3 on the Shelf 1 and the B Bottle rail 1. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Center F Bottle divider 1: 5 1/16" from the inside face of E Left upright and 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 2. Square a pencil line across D Shelf 1 at each mark and stand the divider on it. Center F Bottle divider 2: 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 1 and 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 3. Center F Bottle divider 3: 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 2 and 5 1/16" from the inside face of E Right upright. rows.cuts: 2|36|1.05|1.05|Rail||3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe;2|24|1.05|1.05|Upright||3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe;2|6|1.05|1.05|Arm 1||3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe;2|6|1.05|1.05|Arm 2||3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe;2|6|1.05|1.05|Arm 3||3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe
rows.steps:
Read this Spice rack 36" × 24" × 4" before you cut||10 pieces of 3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe. Same Spice rack 36" × 24" × 4", every face in that stock. About 36" × 24" × 6".||The cut list has every length. Nothing is left off.
Lay out the footprint on the bench||Tape a rectangle 36" × 6" on the bench. Mark centerlines both ways. The faces go up from this outline.||A square base keeps every later part true.
Cut every marked length||PVC cutter or a fine hacksaw. Deburr so each end seats in the fitting. The cut list is the full list — same letter is the same cut. 10 pieces: 2 × 36", 2 × 24", 6 × 6".||A ragged end will not bottom out in a slip tee.
Stand the sides — 2 pieces||2 pieces: 2 × 24". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs. Lay the 2 uprights flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the next parts fasten to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: The 2 uprights stand plumb, 24" tall, centers 36" apart.||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Run the rails — 2 pieces||2 pieces: 2 × 36". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs. Set the 2 rails on the 2 uprights. Fasten it with solvent cement, the same cement on the Buy list. Where: The rails lie at 1" and 23" up from the floor (center lines).||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Place the arm 1 — 2 pieces||2 pieces: 2 × 6". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs. Set the 2 arm 1s on the 2 uprights. Fasten it with solvent cement, the same cement on the Buy list. Where: All 2 arm 1s lie 8 3/8" up from the floor (center line).||Nothing on the model is left out of the steps.
Place the arm 2 — 2 pieces||2 pieces: 2 × 6". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs. Set the 2 arm 2s on the 2 uprights. Fasten it with solvent cement, the same cement on the Buy list. Where: All 2 arm 2s lie 13 3/4" up from the floor (center line).||Nothing on the model is left out of the steps.
Place the arm 3 — 2 pieces||2 pieces: 2 × 6". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs. Set the 2 arm 3s on the 2 uprights. Fasten it with solvent cement, the same cement on the Buy list. Where: All 2 arm 3s lie 19 1/4" up from the floor (center line).||Nothing on the model is left out of the steps.
Check plumb and square||Stand it up. Sight the long edges. If a face racks, find the soft joint and re-join it.||A lean now is a lean forever.

Read this Firewood rack 36" × 72" × 12" before you cut||42 pieces of 3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe. Same Firewood rack 36" × 72" × 12", every face in that stock. About 36" × 72" × 12".||The cut list has every length. Nothing is left off.
Lay out the footprint on the bench||Tape a rectangle 36" × 12" on the bench. Mark centerlines both ways. The faces go up from this outline.||A square base keeps every later part true.
Cut every marked length||PVC cutter or a fine hacksaw. Deburr so each end seats in the fitting. The cut list is the full list — same letter is the same cut. 42 pieces: 12 × 34 3/8", 4 × 18 1/2", 4 × 17 3/4", 8 × 17 5/8", 8 × 11", 2 × 3 3/4", 4 × 3 5/8".||A ragged end will not bottom out in a slip tee.
Stand the sides — 16 pieces||16 pieces: 4 × 18 1/2", 4 × 17 3/4", 8 × 17 5/8". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs.||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Run the rails — 26 pieces||26 pieces: 12 × 34 3/8", 8 × 11", 2 × 3 3/4", 4 × 3 5/8". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs.||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Check plumb and square||Stand it up. Sight the long edges. If a face racks, find the soft joint and re-join it.||A lean now is a lean forever.

Confirm the footprint before the first cut||Firewood rack. Unit 96" wide × 36" deep × 72" high. Freestanding rectangle. Mark the footprint on the floor. Check it is square. 13 parts on this list. Assumed 36" deep (default size) — type a depth to lock it. A free-standing frame of 72" needs a base at least half that, front to back.||If a number on this plan disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list. Geometry is from the bench, not from the prompt's adjectives.
Cut the 2×4 pressure-treated (8 ft)||Hand saw or circular saw. Square every cut. Predrill near the ends — boards split. 3 Sleepers 36 × 3 1/2 × 1 1/2". 1 A Base rail back 96 × 3 1/2 × 1 1/2". 1 B Base rail front 96 × 3 1/2 × 1 1/2". 4 Uprights 70 1/2 × 3 1/2 × 1 1/2". 2 Top tie left layers 15 1/2 × 3 1/2 × 1 1/2". 2 Top tie right layers 15 1/2 × 3 1/2 × 1 1/2". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Board ends split. Predrill.
Glue up the thick parts||E Top tie left: 2 layers of 2×4 pressure-treated (8 ft); F Top tie right: 2 layers of 2×4 pressure-treated (8 ft). Spread glue on each face, stack the layers with the edges flush, clamp them flat and let them cure before shaping or drilling.||
Set the 3 sleepers||Set the D Sleeper 3 on the floor, square to the marks. It is the base the next parts fasten to. Set the D Sleeper 2 on the floor, square to the marks. It is the base the next parts fasten to. Set the D Sleeper 1 on the floor, square to the marks. It is the base the next parts fasten to. Where: Tops of all 3 D sleepers sit 1 1/2" up from the floor.||
Set the Base rail front||Set the B Base rail front on the 3 sleepers. Fasten it with #8 x 2 1/2" exterior screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Top edge of B Base rail front sits 5" up from the floor. Drive 6 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||
Set the Upright right front||Set the Upright right front on the D Sleeper 3 and the B Base rail front. Fasten it with #8 x 2 1/2" exterior screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Drive 4 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||
Set the Upright left front||Set the Upright left front on the D Sleeper 1 and the B Base rail front. Fasten it with #8 x 2 1/2" exterior screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Drive 4 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||
Set the Base rail back||Set the A Base rail back on the 3 sleepers. Fasten it with #8 x 2 1/2" exterior screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Top edge of A Base rail back sits 5" up from the floor. Drive 6 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||
Set the Upright right back||Set the Upright right back on the D Sleeper 3 and the A Base rail back. Fasten it with #8 x 2 1/2" exterior screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Drive 4 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||
Fasten the Top tie right||Fasten the F Top tie right to both C uprights with #8 x 2 1/2" exterior screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Top edge of F Top tie right sits 72" up from the floor — flush with the tops of both C uprights. Outside face flush with the outside of both C uprights. Drive 4 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||
Set the Upright left back||Set the Upright left back on the D Sleeper 1 and the A Base rail back. Fasten it with #8 x 2 1/2" exterior screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Drive 4 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||
Fasten the Top tie left||Fasten the E Top tie left to both C uprights with #8 x 2 1/2" exterior screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Top edge of E Top tie left sits 72" up from the floor — flush with the tops of both C uprights. Outside face flush with the outside of both C uprights. Drive 4 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 36 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||
Seal it for outdoors — finish and end grain||Sand to 180 grit and wipe off the dust. Seal the end grain first: brush finish onto the bottom edges where it meets the ground and every other cut end, let it soak in, and add coats until the end grain stops drinking — end grain wicks water up into the wood. Then brush three coats of exterior finish (spar urethane or exterior oil) on every face, inside and out, with a light sand between coats.||Titebond III and exterior-coated or stainless screws are on the Buy list for every joint. Refresh the finish each spring.
Level it||Level the unit. Check both diagonals match so the frame stays square. If it sits on a floor that is out, shim the feet, keeping the main box square.||Guidance only — confirm the real footprint before you cut. Not stamped engineering.

Where: Tops of the C shelves sit 3/4", 11 3/4" and 22 3/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 11" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both D uprights before you set any shelf. Front edge flush with the front of both D uprights. Top edges of the B jar lips sit 2", 13" and 24" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 11" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on both D uprights before you fix any jar lip. Front face flush with the front of both D uprights. The 2 uprights stand plumb, 30" tall, centers 36" apart. The rails lie at 1" and 29" up from the floor (center lines). All 2 arm 1s lie 10 1/2" up from the floor (center line). All 2 arm 2s lie 17 1/4" up from the floor (center line). All 2 arm 3s lie 24" up from the floor (center line).||If a part is missing from the model, it is missing from the cut list too. Do not build only the first noun.
Cut every part on the list||Left upright, Right upright, Shelf 1, Jar lip 1, Shelf 2, Jar lip 2, Shelf 3, Jar lip 3, Back. Cut each one to the size in its name. Label them with the product they belong to before you mix the piles.||Trust the cut list over a rounded number in this sentence.
Stand the base||Build the floor piece first — uprights, seat or top, shelves, drawers. Leave the tall sides long if they run up to a second piece. Lay the Left upright flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the next parts fasten to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built.||Check the diagonals before the glue skins.
Attach the other product||Fasten the second piece where the model shows it: on the A back and up high for a rack, frame, or mirror, or beside the base when both sit on the floor. Screw the rail or shelf into the tall sides. Lay the C Shelf 1 and Back flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the rest fastens to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built.||A coat rack has to clear a person's shoulders. Do not screw it down on the seat.
Set the jar lips and shelves||Fasten the B Jar lip 1 to both D uprights and the C Shelf 1. Fasten the C Shelf 2 and Shelf 3 to both D uprights. Fasten each one with solvent cement, the same cement on the Buy list.||Each layer goes on after the parts it rests on.
Set the jar lips||Fasten the B Jar lip 2 to both D uprights and the C Shelf 2. Fasten the B Jar lip 3 to both D uprights and the C Shelf 3. Fasten each one with solvent cement, the same cement on the Buy list.||Each layer goes on after the parts it rests on.
Screw it to the wall studs||Hold it level on the wall where it lives and find two studs behind it with a stud finder. Predrill through the Back and drive 4 × 3" structural screws into the studs, 2 per stud. Load nothing onto it until every screw is in a stud.||

rows.steps:
Confirm the footprint before the first cut||Shoe rack. Unit 36" wide × 12" deep × 18" high. Freestanding rectangle. Mark the footprint on the floor. Check it is square. 8 parts on this list. Assumed 36" wide (shoe rack class default) — type a width to lock it. Assumed 18" tall (shoe rack class default) — type a height to lock it. Assumed 12" deep (shoe rack class default) — type a depth to lock it.||If a number on this plan disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list. Geometry is from the bench, not from the prompt's adjectives.
Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8 and 1/4" plywood (backer)||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). From the 3/4" Plywood 4×8: 1 Left upright 18 × 12 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 18 × 12 × 3/4". 1 B Bottom 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". 1 C Shoe shelf 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". 1 D Top 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". 2 Cubby dividers 16 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". From the 1/4" plywood (backer): 1 A Back 34 1/2 × 18 × 1/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Stand the main box||Lay the two E uprights on edge. E Left upright — 18 × 12 × 3/4"; E Right upright — 18 × 12 × 3/4". One join: attach B Bottom to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Where: Top of B Bottom sits 3/4" up from the floor — flush with the bottom ends of both E uprights. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. In all, this step drives 24 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws, from the model's joints.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Attach D Top to both E uprights||One join: attach D Top to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Where: Top of D Top sits 18" up from the floor — flush with the top ends of both E uprights. Its underside rests on the top of both F cubby dividers, 17 1/4" up from the floor. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. These screws are counted in another step's total.||One join at a time — dry-fit, then glue and drive the screws for this join only.
Set cubby dividers||F Cubby divider 1 — 16 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4"; F Cubby divider 2 — 16 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". Space them evenly. Screw through the D top, bottom, and back into each divider. Where: F Cubby divider 1 stands 10 7/8" from the inside face of E Left upright and 11 1/4" from F Cubby divider 2. Square a pencil line across B Bottom at each mark and stand the divider on it. F Cubby divider 2 stands 11 1/4" from F Cubby divider 1 and 10 7/8" from the inside face of E Right upright. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||
Attach A Back to the back of the box||One join: attach A Back to the back edges of both E Uprights, B Bottom and D Top and both F Cubby dividers with 22 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws, one about every 8" along each edge. Square the box first: both diagonals measure the same. Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. These screws are counted in another step's total.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Glue 1 fixed shelf||C Shoe shelf — 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into each shelf at those marked heights. Square every bay. The back is already on and square: slide each shelf in to touch it, then drive 5 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws through A Back into the shelf back edges, one about every 8". These shelves are fixed — no pins. Where: Top of C Shoe shelf sits 8 5/8" up from the top of B Bottom (9 3/8" from the floor). Mark 8 5/8" up from the top of B Bottom on the inside face of both E uprights and line the top face up with the marks. Or cut a spacer block 7 7/8" long, stand it on B Bottom, and rest the part on it while you fasten it. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Drive 13 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 51 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Wipe squeeze-out.
Level it||Level the unit. The A back is already on it so the box stays square. If it sits on a floor that is out, shim the feet, keeping the main box square.||Guidance only — confirm the real footprint before you cut. Not stamped engineering.

rows.steps:
Read this Shoe rack before you cut||58 pieces of 3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe. Same Shoe rack, every face in that stock. About 36" × 18" × 12".||The cut list has every length. Nothing is left off.
Lay out the footprint on the bench||Tape a rectangle 36" × 12" on the bench. Mark centerlines both ways. The faces go up from this outline.||A square base keeps every later part true.
Cut every marked length||PVC cutter or a fine hacksaw. Deburr so each end seats in the fitting. The cut list is the full list — same letter is the same cut. 58 pieces: 8 × 12", 16 × 11 1/4", 6 × 11", 16 × 8 3/8", 4 × 3 7/8", 8 × 3 5/8".||A ragged end will not bottom out in a slip tee.
Stand the sides — 16 pieces||16 pieces: 16 × 8 3/8". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs.||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Run the rails — 42 pieces||42 pieces: 8 × 12", 16 × 11 1/4", 6 × 11", 4 × 3 7/8", 8 × 3 5/8". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs.||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Check plumb and square||Stand it up. Sight the long edges. If a face racks, find the soft joint and re-join it.||A lean now is a lean forever.

Confirm the hang before the first cut||Wine rack. Wall-mounted wine rack 24" wide × 12" deep × 36" high. Holds about 42 bottles — 7 rows of about 6 bottles each, lying side by side on open shelves (rows on a 4 1/2" pitch, one bottle high). The bottle rows sit on a 3 3/4" plinth, recessed like a kick strip, so the top cap lands at the full 36" height. This hangs on the wall, so the layout marks go on the wall. Find two studs. Typical bottom sits about 36–42" off the floor, or sit it on a counter and still screw it into the studs with 3" structural screws so it stays upright. 19 parts on this list. Assumed 24" wide (default size) — type a width to lock it. Assumed 36" tall (default size) — type a height to lock it. Assumed 12" deep (default size) — type a depth to lock it.||This is a wine rack, not a bookcase. Bottles lie on their sides. If a number disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). 1 Left upright 36 × 12 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 36 × 12 × 3/4". 1 D Plinth 22 1/2 × 3 3/4 × 3/4". 8 shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 7 Bottle rails 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". 1 A Back 36 × 22 1/2 × 3/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Set the Plinth||Lay the Plinth flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the next parts fasten to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: Top edge of D Plinth sits 3 3/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. Front face set back 3 1/2" from the front of both B uprights.||This part was on the model and not yet in a step.
Stand the rack||B Left upright — 36 × 12 × 3/4"; B Right upright — 36 × 12 × 3/4". A Back — 36 × 22 1/2 × 3/4". E Shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 2 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 3 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 4 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 5 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 6 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 7 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 8 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Marked heights: E Shelf 1 at 3 3/4" from the bottom; E Shelf 2 at 8 1/4" from the bottom; E Shelf 3 at 12 3/4" from the bottom; E Shelf 4 at 17 1/4" from the bottom; E Shelf 5 at 21 3/4" from the bottom; E Shelf 6 at 26 1/4" from the bottom; E Shelf 7 at 30 3/4" from the bottom; E Shelf 8 at 35 1/4" from the bottom. Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into each E shelf at those marked heights. Use fixed shelves here, screwed in place — a row of bottles is heavy. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Lay the Left upright, Right upright and Back flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the rest fastens to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first rack.
Set the shelves||Fasten the E Shelf 1, Shelf 2, Shelf 3, Shelf 4, Shelf 5, Shelf 6, Shelf 7 and Shelf 8 to both B uprights. Fasten each one with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Tops of the E shelves sit 4 1/2", 9", 13 1/2", 18", 22 1/2", 27", 31 1/2" and 36" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 4 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both B uprights before you set any shelf. Or cut a spacer block 3 3/4" long, stand it on the bottom edge, and rest the lowest shelf on it. Front edge flush with the front of both B uprights. Drive 59 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Each layer goes on after the parts it rests on.
Glue the bottle rails||C Bottle rail 1 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; C Bottle rail 2 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; C Bottle rail 3 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; C Bottle rail 4 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; C Bottle rail 5 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; C Bottle rail 6 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; C Bottle rail 7 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". Glue a 1 1/2" rail on the front of every shelf that carries a row of bottles so they stay on. #8 × 1 1/4" screws from behind the rail into the shelf front edge. Drive 49 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 122 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||The rail stands on the front edge of the E shelf. Wipe squeeze-out before it skins. Bottles lie on their sides, necks facing out.
Hang it on studs||Find two studs. Predrill the A back. Drive 3" structural screws through the A back into the studs — 4 to 6 screws. A loaded wine rack will rip off drywall anchors.||Guidance only — hit a stud. Confirm the hang height so you can reach a bottle.

Holds 12 bottles, with 2 open shelves above — 3 rows × 4 across, one opening per bottle (rows on a 4 1/2" pitch, one bottle high). Above the bottles: 2 open shelves, 10 1/8" clear each, for glasses, decanters or books — capped at the 36" height you typed. This hangs on the wall, so the layout marks go on the wall. Find two studs. Typical bottom sits about 36–42" off the floor, or sit it on a counter and still screw it into the studs with 3" structural screws so it stays upright. 15 parts on this list. Assumed 24" wide (default size) — type a width to lock it.||This is a wine rack, not a bookcase. Bottles lie on their sides. If a number disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Glue up and cut the Oak 1×4||Glue-up first: parts wider than one Oak 1×4 (3 1/2" face) are edge-glued from boards laid side by side — Left upright (4 boards, 37" long); Right upright (4 boards, 37" long); 4 × Shelf (4 boards, 23 1/2" long); 2 × Grid shelf (4 boards, 23 1/2" long); 3 × Divider (4 boards, 13 3/4" long); A Back (7 boards, 37" long). Joint the edges straight, glue and clamp every 12", let it cure overnight, then rip to width and cut to length. Hand saw or circular saw. Square every cut. Predrill near the ends — boards split. 1 Left upright 36 × 12 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 36 × 12 × 3/4". 4 shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 3 Bottle rails 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". 2 Grid shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 3 Dividers 12 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". 1 A Back 36 × 22 1/2 × 3/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack. Where: Tops of the D grid shelves sit 5 1/4" and 9 3/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 4 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both B uprights before you set any grid shelf. Or cut a spacer block 4 1/2" long, stand it on the bottom edge, and rest the lowest grid shelf on it. Front edge flush with the front of both B uprights. Center F Bottle divider 1: 5 1/16" from the inside face of B Left upright and 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 2. Square a pencil line across E Shelf 1 at each mark and stand the divider on it. Center F Bottle divider 2: 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 1 and 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 3. Center F Bottle divider 3: 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 2 and 5 1/16" from the inside face of B Right upright.||Board ends split. Predrill.
Stand the rack||B Left upright — 36 × 12 × 3/4"; B Right upright — 36 × 12 × 3/4". A Back — 36 × 22 1/2 × 3/4". E Shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 4 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Open shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 6 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into every shelf at those marked heights. Then screw the bottom shelf and the shelf above the bottle rows into the divider ends, and the A back onto the shelf edges. Use fixed shelves here, screwed in place — a row of bottles is heavy. Predrill near the ends so the wood does not split. Lay the Left upright, Right upright, Shelf 1 and Back flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the rest fastens to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: Tops of the E shelves sit 3/4", 14 1/4", 25 1/8" and 36" up from the bottom edge of the unit. Gaps top to top: 13 1/2", 10 7/8" and 10 7/8". Mark every height on the inside face of both B uprights before you set any shelf. Front edge flush with the front of both B uprights. Drive 17 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Every opening should take a bottle with room to spare.
Set the shelves and open shelves||Fasten the Shelf 4, Open shelf 1 and Shelf 6 to both B uprights. Fasten each one with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Drive 21 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Each layer goes on after the parts it rests on.
Notch and slot the bottle grid||. D Grid shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; D Grid shelf 2 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Dividers: cut 2 notches 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the front edge, one where each shelf crosses, at 3 3/4" and 8 1/4" up from the bottom end. Middle shelves: cut 3 notches 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the back edge, one at each divider crossing, at 5 1/16", 10 7/8" and 16 11/16" from the left end. Saw both sides of each notch and chisel out the waste. Slot every divider down over the middle shelves so the front edges line up — an egg-crate grid. Dry-fit, then glue the laps. Fasten the D Grid shelf 1 to both B uprights with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Cut one notch, test it on a scrap of the same board, then cut the rest. A snug hand-press fit is right — no hammering.
Glue the bottle rails||C Bottle rail 1 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; C Bottle rail 2 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; C Bottle rail 3 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". Glue a 1 1/2" rail on the front of every shelf that carries a row of bottles so they stay on. #8 × 1 1/4" screws from behind the rail into the shelf front edge. Drive 21 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||The rail stands on the front edge of the shelf. Wipe squeeze-out before it skins. Bottles lie on their sides, necks facing out.
Set the Bottle divider 1, Bottle divider 2 and Bottle divider 3||Set the Bottle divider 1 on the Shelf 1 and the C Bottle rail 1. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Set the Bottle divider 2 on the Shelf 1 and the C Bottle rail 1. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Set the Bottle divider 3 on the Shelf 1 and the C Bottle rail 1. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Drive 48 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 121 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||It goes on once every part under it is in place.

rows.prompt: pvc pine wine rack for 15 bottles 20 inches tall
rows.buy: 12×Pine 1×4=48; 3×#8 x 1-1/4" wood screws=25.41; 1×Wood glue=4.98; 1×GRK RSS #9 x 3-1/8 structural screws=18.97
rows.cuts: 1|22.5|20|0.75|Back||Pine 1×4;3|22.5|1.5|0.75|Bottle rail|Scalloped cradle: 5 scallops 3 1/2" wide, cut down to 3/16" of rail, one centred on each bottle. Trace the arcs from the plan and cut with a jigsaw.|Pine 1×4;2|22.5|11.25|0.75|Grid shelf|Egg-crate half-lap: cut 4 notches 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the back edge, one at each divider crossing, at 3 7/8", 8 9/16", 13 3/16" and 17 7/8" from the left end.|Pine 1×4;1|22.5|5.75|0.75|Plinth||Pine 1×4;2|22.5|11.25|0.75|Shelf||Pine 1×4;2|20|12|0.75|Upright||Pine 1×4;4|12.75|10.5|0.75|Divider|Egg-crate half-lap: cut 2 notches 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the front edge, one where each shelf crosses, at 3 3/4" and 8 1/4" up from the bottom end.|Pine 1×4
rows.steps:
Confirm the hang before the first cut||Pine Wine rack. Wall-mounted wine rack 24" wide × 12" deep × 20" high. Holds 15 bottles — 3 rows × 5 across, one opening per bottle (rows on a 4 1/2" pitch, one bottle high). The bottle rows sit on a 5 3/4" plinth, recessed like a kick strip, so the top cap lands at the 20" height you typed. This hangs on the wall, so the layout marks go on the wall. Find two studs. Typical bottom sits about 36–42" off the floor, or sit it on a counter and still screw it into the studs with 3" structural screws so it stays upright. 15 parts on this list. Assumed 24" wide (default size) — type a width to lock it. Assumed 12" deep (default size) — type a depth to lock it.||This is a wine rack, not a bookcase. Bottles lie on their sides. If a number disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Glue up and cut the Pine 1×4||Glue-up first: parts wider than one Pine 1×4 (3 1/2" face) are edge-glued from boards laid side by side — Left upright (4 boards, 21" long); Right upright (4 boards, 21" long); D Plinth (2 boards, 23 1/2" long); 2 × Shelf (4 boards, 23 1/2" long); 2 × Grid shelf (4 boards, 23 1/2" long); 4 × Divider (4 boards, 13 3/4" long); A Back (6 boards, 23 1/2" long). Joint the edges straight, glue and clamp every 12", let it cure overnight, then rip to width and cut to length. Hand saw or circular saw. Square every cut. Predrill near the ends — boards split. 1 Left upright 20 × 12 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 20 × 12 × 3/4". 1 D Plinth 22 1/2 × 5 3/4 × 3/4". 2 shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 3 Bottle rails 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". 2 Grid shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 4 Dividers 12 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". 1 A Back 22 1/2 × 20 × 3/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack. Where: Tops of the C grid shelves sit 11" and 15 1/2" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 4 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both F uprights before you set any grid shelf. Or cut a spacer block 10 1/4" long, stand it on the bottom edge, and rest the lowest grid shelf on it. Front edge flush with the front of both F uprights. Top edge of D Plinth sits 5 3/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. Front face set back 3 1/2" from the front of both F uprights. Center G Bottle divider 1: 3 7/8" from the inside face of F Left upright and 3 7/8" from G Bottle divider 2. Square a pencil line across E Shelf 1 at each mark and stand the divider on it. Center G Bottle divider 2: 3 7/8" from G Bottle divider 1 and 3 7/8" from G Bottle divider 3. Center G Bottle divider 3: 3 7/8" from G Bottle divider 2 and 3 7/8" from G Bottle divider 4. Center G Bottle divider 4: 3 7/8" from G Bottle divider 3 and 3 7/8" from the inside face of F Right upright.||Board ends split. Predrill.
Stand the rack||F Left upright — 20 × 12 × 3/4"; F Right upright — 20 × 12 × 3/4". A Back — 22 1/2 × 20 × 3/4". E Shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 4 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Marked heights: Shelf 1 at 5 3/4" from the bottom; C Grid shelf 1 at 10 1/4" from the bottom; C Grid shelf 2 at 14 3/4" from the bottom; Shelf 4 at 19 1/4" from the bottom. Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into every shelf at those marked heights. Then screw the bottom shelf and the shelf above the bottle rows into the divider ends, and the A back onto the shelf edges. D Plinth — 22 1/2 × 5 3/4 × 3/4": glue and screw the D plinth between the uprights under the bottom shelf, recessed 3 1/2" from the front — the recessed base keeps the front clean and lifts the rows so the top cap lands at the full height. Use fixed shelves here, screwed in place — a row of bottles is heavy. Predrill near the ends so the wood does not split. Lay the Left upright, Right upright, Plinth and Back flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the rest fastens to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Drive 10 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Every opening should take a bottle with room to spare.
Notch and slot the bottle grid||G Bottle divider 1 — 12 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4"; G Bottle divider 2 — 12 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4"; G Bottle divider 3 — 12 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4"; G Bottle divider 4 — 12 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". C Grid shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; C Grid shelf 2 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Dividers: cut 2 notches 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the front edge, one where each shelf crosses, at 3 3/4" and 8 1/4" up from the bottom end. Middle shelves: cut 4 notches 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the back edge, one at each divider crossing, at 3 7/8", 8 9/16", 13 3/16" and 17 7/8" from the left end. Saw both sides of each notch and chisel out the waste. Slot every divider down over the middle shelves so the front edges line up — an egg-crate grid. Dry-fit, then glue the laps. Fasten the C Grid shelf 1 and Grid shelf 2 to both F uprights. Fasten each one with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Cut one notch, test it on a scrap of the same board, then cut the rest. A snug hand-press fit is right — no hammering.
Set the shelves||Fasten the Shelf 1 and Shelf 4 to both F uprights. Fasten each one with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Tops of the E shelves sit 6 1/2" and 20" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 13 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both F uprights before you set any shelf. Or cut a spacer block 5 3/4" long, stand it on the bottom edge, and rest the lowest shelf on it. Front edge flush with the front of both F uprights. Drive 17 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Each layer goes on after the parts it rests on.
Glue the bottle rails||B Bottle rail 1 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; B Bottle rail 2 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; B Bottle rail 3 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". Glue a 1 1/2" rail on the front of every shelf that carries a row of bottles so they stay on. #8 × 1 1/4" screws from behind the rail into the shelf front edge. Drive 21 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||The rail stands on the front edge of the shelf. Wipe squeeze-out before it skins. Bottles lie on their sides, necks facing out.
Set the bottle dividers||Set the Bottle divider 1, Bottle divider 2, Bottle divider 3 and Bottle divider 4 on the Shelf 1 and the B Bottle rail 1. Fasten each one with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Drive 64 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 126 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||Each layer goes on after the parts it rests on.
Hang it on studs||Find two studs. Predrill the A back. Drive 3" structural screws through the A back into the studs — 4 to 6 screws. A loaded wine rack will rip off drywall anchors.||Guidance only — hit a stud. Confirm the hang height so you can reach a bottle.

rows.steps:
Confirm the footprint before the first cut||Shoe rack. Unit 36" wide × 12" deep × 21" high. Freestanding rectangle. Mark the footprint on the floor. Check it is square. 8 parts on this list. Assumed 36" wide (shoe rack class default) — type a width to lock it. Assumed 21" tall on its casters (shoe rack class default) — type a height to lock it. Assumed 12" deep (shoe rack class default) — type a depth to lock it.||If a number on this plan disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list. Geometry is from the bench, not from the prompt's adjectives.
Cut the 1/4" plywood 4x8 (backer) and 3/4" Plywood 4×8||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). From the 1/4" plywood 4x8 (backer): 1 A Back 34 1/2 × 18 × 1/4". From the 3/4" Plywood 4×8: 1 B Bottom 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". 1 C Shoe shelf 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". 1 D Top 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". 2 E Upright 18 × 12 × 3/4". 2 F Cubby divider 16 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Stand the main box||Lay the two E uprights on edge. E Left upright — 18 × 12 × 3/4"; E Right upright — 18 × 12 × 3/4". One join: attach B Bottom to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Where: Top of B Bottom sits 3 3/4" up from the floor — flush with the bottom ends of both E uprights. Its underside rests on the top of the caster 1, the caster 2, the caster 3 and the caster 4, 3" up from the floor. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. In all, this step drives 24 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws, from the model's joints.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Attach D Top to both E uprights||One join: attach D Top to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Where: Top of D Top sits 21" up from the floor — flush with the top ends of both E uprights. Its underside rests on the top of both F cubby dividers, 20 1/4" up from the floor. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. These screws are counted in another step's total.||One join at a time — dry-fit, then glue and drive the screws for this join only.
Set cubby dividers||F Cubby divider 1 — 16 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4"; F Cubby divider 2 — 16 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". Space them evenly. Screw through the D top, bottom, and back into each divider. Where: F Cubby divider 1 stands 10 7/8" from the inside face of E Left upright and 11 1/4" from F Cubby divider 2. Square a pencil line across B Bottom at each mark and stand the divider on it. F Cubby divider 2 stands 11 1/4" from F Cubby divider 1 and 10 7/8" from the inside face of E Right upright. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||
Glue 1 fixed shelf||C Shoe shelf — 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into each shelf at those marked heights. Square every bay. The back is already on and square: slide each shelf in to touch it, then drive 5 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws through A Back into the shelf back edges, one about every 8". These shelves are fixed — no pins. Where: Top of C Shoe shelf sits 8 5/8" up from the top of B Bottom (12 3/8" from the floor). Mark 8 5/8" up from the top of B Bottom on the inside face of both E uprights and line the top face up with the marks. Or cut a spacer block 7 7/8" long, stand it on B Bottom, and rest the part on it while you fasten it. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Drive 13 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Wipe squeeze-out.
Screw on the 4 casters||Tip the piece on its side. Screw each caster under its corner with four #10 × 3/4" pan-head screws through its plate, 1/2" in from the edges; the two locking casters go at the front. Stand it up and lock them. Where: Top edge of Caster 1 sits 3" up from the floor. Front face flush with the front of E. Top edge of Caster 2 sits 3" up from the floor. Front face flush with the front of E. Top edge of Caster 3 sits 3" up from the floor. Back face flush with the back of E. Top edge of Caster 4 sits 3" up from the floor. Back face flush with the back of E. Drive 20 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 71 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||
Attach A Back to the back of the box||One join: attach A Back to the back edges of both E Uprights, B Bottom, C Shoe shelf and D Top and both F Cubby dividers with 22 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws, one about every 8" along each edge. Square the box first: both diagonals measure the same. Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. These screws are counted in another step's total.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Level it||Level the unit. The A back is already on it so the box stays square. If it sits on a floor that is out, shim the feet, keeping the main box square.||Guidance only — confirm the real footprint before you cut. Not stamped engineering.

Lay out the footprint on the bench||Tape a rectangle 36" × 12" on the bench. Mark centerlines both ways. The faces go up from this outline.||A square base keeps every later part true.
Cut every marked length||PVC cutter or a fine hacksaw. Deburr so each end seats in the fitting. The cut list is the full list — same letter is the same cut. 58 pieces: 8 × 12", 16 × 11 1/4", 6 × 11", 16 × 8 3/8", 4 × 3 7/8", 8 × 3 5/8".||A ragged end will not bottom out in a slip tee.
Stand the sides — 16 pieces||16 pieces: 16 × 8 3/8". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs.||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Run the rails — 42 pieces||42 pieces: 8 × 12", 16 × 11 1/4", 6 × 11", 4 × 3 7/8", 8 × 3 5/8". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs.||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Check plumb and square||Stand it up. Sight the long edges. If a face racks, find the soft joint and re-join it.||A lean now is a lean forever.

rows.cuts: 1|33|18|0.25|Back||1/4" plywood 4x8 (backer);1|33|11.75|1.5|Bottom||2×2 (8 ft);1|33|11.75|1.5|Shoe shelf|Egg-crate half-lap: cut 2 notches 1 1/2" wide × 5 7/8" deep from the back edge, one at each divider crossing, at 9 3/4" and 21 3/4" from the left end.|2×2 (8 ft);1|33|11.75|1.5|Top||2×2 (8 ft);2|18|12|1.5|Upright||2×2 (8 ft);2|15|11.75|1.5|Cubby divider|Egg-crate half-lap: cut a notch 1 1/2" wide × 5 7/8" deep from the front edge, one where each shelf crosses, at 6 3/8" up from the bottom end.|2×2 (8 ft)
rows.steps:
Confirm the footprint before the first cut||Shoe rack. Unit 36" wide × 12" deep × 18" high. Freestanding rectangle. Mark the footprint on the floor. Check it is square. 8 parts on this list. Assumed 36" wide (shoe rack class default) — type a width to lock it. Assumed 18" tall (shoe rack class default) — type a height to lock it. Assumed 12" deep (shoe rack class default) — type a depth to lock it.||If a number on this plan disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list. Geometry is from the bench, not from the prompt's adjectives.
Cut the 2×2 (8 ft) and 1/4" plywood (backer)||Hand saw or circular saw. Square every cut. Predrill near the ends — boards split. From the 2×2 (8 ft): 1 Left upright 18 × 12 × 1 1/2". 1 Right upright 18 × 12 × 1 1/2". 1 B Bottom 33 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". 1 C Shoe shelf 33 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". 1 D Top 33 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". 2 Cubby dividers 15 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". From the 1/4" plywood (backer): 1 A Back 33 × 18 × 1/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Board ends split. Predrill.
Stand the main box||Lay the two E uprights on edge. E Left upright — 18 × 12 × 1 1/2"; E Right upright — 18 × 12 × 1 1/2". One join: attach B Bottom to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the wood does not split. Where: Top of B Bottom sits 1 1/2" up from the floor — flush with the bottom ends of both E uprights. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. In all, this step drives 24 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws, from the model's joints.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Attach D Top to both E uprights||One join: attach D Top to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the wood does not split. Where: Top of D Top sits 18" up from the floor — flush with the top ends of both E uprights. Its underside rests on the top of both F cubby dividers, 16 1/2" up from the floor. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. These screws are counted in another step's total.||One join at a time — dry-fit, then glue and drive the screws for this join only.
Set cubby dividers||F Cubby divider 1 — 15 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2"; F Cubby divider 2 — 15 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". Space them evenly. Screw through the D top, bottom, and back into each divider. Where: F Cubby divider 1 stands 9 3/4" from the inside face of E Left upright and 10 1/2" from F Cubby divider 2. Square a pencil line across B Bottom at each mark and stand the divider on it. F Cubby divider 2 stands 10 1/2" from F Cubby divider 1 and 9 3/4" from the inside face of E Right upright. Drive 12 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||
Attach A Back to the back of the box||One join: attach A Back to the back edges of both E Uprights, B Bottom and D Top and both F Cubby dividers with 20 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws, one about every 8" along each edge. Square the box first: both diagonals measure the same. Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the wood does not split. These screws are counted in another step's total.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Glue 1 fixed shelf||C Shoe shelf — 33 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". Glue and #8 × 2 1/2" screws through the uprights into each shelf at those marked heights. Square every bay. The back is already on and square: slide each shelf in to touch it, then drive 5 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws through A Back into the shelf back edges, one about every 8". These shelves are fixed — no pins. Where: Top of C Shoe shelf sits 7 7/8" up from the top of B Bottom (9 3/8" from the floor). Mark 7 7/8" up from the top of B Bottom on the inside face of both E uprights and line the top face up with the marks. Or cut a spacer block 6 3/8" long, stand it on B Bottom, and rest the part on it while you fasten it. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Drive 9 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 45 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||Predrill near the ends so the wood does not split. Wipe squeeze-out.
Level it||Level the unit. The A back is already on it so the box stays square. If it sits on a floor that is out, shim the feet, keeping the main box square.||Guidance only — confirm the real footprint before you cut. Not stamped engineering.

Cut the 2×2 (8 ft) and 1/4" plywood (backer)||Hand saw or circular saw. Square every cut. Predrill near the ends — boards split. From the 2×2 (8 ft): 1 Left upright 18 × 12 × 1 1/2". 1 Right upright 18 × 12 × 1 1/2". 1 B Bottom 33 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". 1 C Shoe shelf 33 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". 1 D Top 33 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". 2 Cubby dividers 15 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". From the 1/4" plywood (backer): 1 A Back 33 × 18 × 1/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Board ends split. Predrill.
Stand the main box||Lay the two E uprights on edge. E Left upright — 18 × 12 × 1 1/2"; E Right upright — 18 × 12 × 1 1/2". One join: attach B Bottom to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the wood does not split. Where: Top of B Bottom sits 1 1/2" up from the floor — flush with the bottom ends of both E uprights. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. In all, this step drives 24 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws, from the model's joints.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Attach D Top to both E uprights||One join: attach D Top to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the wood does not split. Where: Top of D Top sits 18" up from the floor — flush with the top ends of both E uprights. Its underside rests on the top of both F cubby dividers, 16 1/2" up from the floor. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. These screws are counted in another step's total.||One join at a time — dry-fit, then glue and drive the screws for this join only.
Set cubby dividers||F Cubby divider 1 — 15 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2"; F Cubby divider 2 — 15 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". Space them evenly. Screw through the D top, bottom, and back into each divider. Where: F Cubby divider 1 stands 9 3/4" from the inside face of E Left upright and 10 1/2" from F Cubby divider 2. Square a pencil line across B Bottom at each mark and stand the divider on it. F Cubby divider 2 stands 10 1/2" from F Cubby divider 1 and 9 3/4" from the inside face of E Right upright. Drive 12 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||
Attach A Back to the back of the box||One join: attach A Back to the back edges of both E Uprights, B Bottom and D Top and both F Cubby dividers with 20 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws, one about every 8" along each edge. Square the box first: both diagonals measure the same. Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the wood does not split. These screws are counted in another step's total.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Glue 1 fixed shelf||C Shoe shelf — 33 × 11 3/4 × 1 1/2". Glue and #8 × 2 1/2" screws through the uprights into each shelf at those marked heights. Square every bay. The back is already on and square: slide each shelf in to touch it, then drive 5 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws through A Back into the shelf back edges, one about every 8". These shelves are fixed — no pins. Where: Top of C Shoe shelf sits 7 7/8" up from the top of B Bottom (9 3/8" from the floor). Mark 7 7/8" up from the top of B Bottom on the inside face of both E uprights and line the top face up with the marks. Or cut a spacer block 6 3/8" long, stand it on B Bottom, and rest the part on it while you fasten it. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Drive 9 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 45 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||Predrill near the ends so the wood does not split. Wipe squeeze-out.
Level it||Level the unit. The A back is already on it so the box stays square. If it sits on a floor that is out, shim the feet, keeping the main box square.||Guidance only — confirm the real footprint before you cut. Not stamped engineering.

rows.cuts: 2|24|1.05|1.05|Upright||3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe;2|18|1.05|1.05|Rail||3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe;2|6|1.05|1.05|Arm 1||3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe;2|6|1.05|1.05|Arm 2||3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe;2|6|1.05|1.05|Arm 3||3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe
rows.steps:
Read this Spice rack 18" × 24" × 4" before you cut||10 pieces of 3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe. Same Spice rack 18" × 24" × 4", every face in that stock. About 18" × 24" × 6".||The cut list has every length. Nothing is left off.
Lay out the footprint on the bench||Tape a rectangle 18" × 6" on the bench. Mark centerlines both ways. The faces go up from this outline.||A square base keeps every later part true.
Cut every marked length||PVC cutter or a fine hacksaw. Deburr so each end seats in the fitting. The cut list is the full list — same letter is the same cut. 10 pieces: 2 × 24", 2 × 18", 6 × 6".||A ragged end will not bottom out in a slip tee.
Stand the sides — 2 pieces||2 pieces: 2 × 24". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs. Lay the 2 uprights flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the next parts fasten to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: The 2 uprights stand plumb, 24" tall, centers 18" apart.||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Run the rails — 2 pieces||2 pieces: 2 × 18". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs. Set the 2 rails on the 2 uprights. Fasten it with solvent cement, the same cement on the Buy list. Where: The rails lie at 1" and 23" up from the bottom (center lines).||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Place the arm 1 — 2 pieces||2 pieces: 2 × 6". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs. Set the 2 arm 1s on the 2 uprights. Fasten it with solvent cement, the same cement on the Buy list. Where: All 2 arm 1s lie 8 3/8" up from the bottom (center line).||Nothing on the model is left out of the steps.
Place the arm 2 — 2 pieces||2 pieces: 2 × 6". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs. Set the 2 arm 2s on the 2 uprights. Fasten it with solvent cement, the same cement on the Buy list. Where: All 2 arm 2s lie 13 3/4" up from the bottom (center line).||Nothing on the model is left out of the steps.
Place the arm 3 — 2 pieces||2 pieces: 2 × 6". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs. Set the 2 arm 3s on the 2 uprights. Fasten it with solvent cement, the same cement on the Buy list. Where: All 2 arm 3s lie 19 1/4" up from the bottom (center line).||Nothing on the model is left out of the steps.
Check plumb and square||Stand it up. Sight the long edges. If a face racks, find the soft joint and re-join it.||A lean now is a lean forever.
