rows.prompt: spice rack 18 wide 24 high 4 deep from 2x2
rows.buy: 6×2×2 (8 ft)=27; 1×#8 x 2-1/2" wood screws=9.47; 1×Wood glue=4.98; 1×GRK RSS #9 x 3-1/8 structural screws=18.97
rows.steps:
Confirm the hang before the first cut||Spice rack. Wall-mounted spice rack 18" wide × 4" deep × 24" high. This hangs on the wall, so the layout marks go on the wall. Find two studs. Typical bottom sits about 48–54" off the floor so jars are at counter height. 9 parts on this list.||This is a wall spice rack, not a floor box. If a number disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Cut the 2×2 (8 ft)||Hand saw or circular saw. Square every cut. Predrill near the ends — boards split. 1 Left upright 24 × 2 1/2 × 1 1/2". 1 Right upright 24 × 2 1/2 × 1 1/2". 1 D Shelf 15 × 1 1/2 × 1". 3 Jar lips 15 × 1 1/2 × 1 1/4". 2 shelves 15 × 2 1/2 × 1 1/2". 1 A Back 24 × 16 1/2 × 1 1/2". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack. Plane or resaw the D shelf, jar lip to the thickness on the list before you cut to length.||Board ends split. Predrill.
Stand the rack||B Left upright — 24 × 2 1/2 × 1 1/2"; B Right upright — 24 × 2 1/2 × 1 1/2". A Back — 24 × 16 1/2 × 1 1/2". D Shelf 1 — 15 × 1 1/2 × 1"; E Shelf 2 — 15 × 2 1/2 × 1 1/2"; E Shelf 3 — 15 × 2 1/2 × 1 1/2". Glue and #8 × 2 1/2" screws through the uprights into each D shelf at those marked heights. Use fixed shelves here, screwed in place — jars are heavy and the lips need a solid shelf. Predrill near the ends so the wood does not split. Lay the Left upright, Right upright, Shelf 1 and Back flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the rest fastens to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: Tops of the E shelves sit 11 3/4" and 22 3/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 11" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both B uprights before you set any shelf. Or cut a spacer block 10 1/4" long, stand it on the bottom edge, and rest the lowest shelf on it. Front edge flush with the front of both B uprights. Drive 12 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first rack.
Set the shelves||Fasten the D Shelf 2 and Shelf 3 to both B uprights. Fasten each one with #8 x 2 1/2" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Drive 12 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Each layer goes on after the parts it rests on.
Glue the jar lips||C Jar lip 1 — 15 × 1 1/2 × 1 1/4"; C Jar lip 2 — 15 × 1 1/2 × 1 1/4"; C Jar lip 3 — 15 × 1 1/2 × 1 1/4". Glue a 1 1/4" jar lip on the front of every shelf so jars stay on. #8 × 2 1/2" screws from behind the lip into the shelf front edge. Fasten the C Jar lip 1 to both B uprights with #8 x 2 1/2" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Tops of the C jar lips sit 2", 13" and 24" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 11" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both B uprights before you set any jar lip. Front edge flush with the front of both B uprights. Drive 18 × #8 × 2 1/2" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 42 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||The lip stands on the front edge of the D shelf. Wipe squeeze-out before it skins.
Hang it on studs||Find two studs. Predrill the A back. Drive 3" structural screws through the A back into the studs — 4 screws. Loaded spice jars will rip off drywall anchors.||Guidance only — hit a stud. Confirm the hang height so jars sit at counter height.

rows.cuts: 2|24|1.05|1.05|Upright||3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe;2|18|1.05|1.05|Rail||3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe;2|6|1.05|1.05|Arm 1||3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe;2|6|1.05|1.05|Arm 2||3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe;2|6|1.05|1.05|Arm 3||3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe
rows.steps:
Read this Spice rack 18" × 24" × 4" before you cut||10 pieces of 3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe. Same Spice rack 18" × 24" × 4", every face in that stock. About 18" × 24" × 6".||The cut list has every length. Nothing is left off.
Lay out the footprint on the bench||Tape a rectangle 18" × 6" on the bench. Mark centerlines both ways. The faces go up from this outline.||A square base keeps every later part true.
Cut every marked length||PVC cutter or a fine hacksaw. Deburr so each end seats in the fitting. The cut list is the full list — same letter is the same cut. 10 pieces: 2 × 24", 2 × 18", 6 × 6".||A ragged end will not bottom out in a slip tee.
Stand the sides — 2 pieces||2 pieces: 2 × 24". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs. Lay the 2 uprights flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the next parts fasten to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: The 2 uprights stand plumb, 24" tall, centers 18" apart.||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Run the rails — 2 pieces||2 pieces: 2 × 18". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs. Set the 2 rails on the 2 uprights. Fasten it with solvent cement, the same cement on the Buy list. Where: The rails lie at 1" and 23" up from the bottom (center lines).||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Place the arm 1 — 2 pieces||2 pieces: 2 × 6". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs. Set the 2 arm 1s on the 2 uprights. Fasten it with solvent cement, the same cement on the Buy list. Where: All 2 arm 1s lie 8 3/8" up from the bottom (center line).||Nothing on the model is left out of the steps.
Place the arm 2 — 2 pieces||2 pieces: 2 × 6". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs. Set the 2 arm 2s on the 2 uprights. Fasten it with solvent cement, the same cement on the Buy list. Where: All 2 arm 2s lie 13 3/4" up from the bottom (center line).||Nothing on the model is left out of the steps.
Place the arm 3 — 2 pieces||2 pieces: 2 × 6". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs. Set the 2 arm 3s on the 2 uprights. Fasten it with solvent cement, the same cement on the Buy list. Where: All 2 arm 3s lie 19 1/4" up from the bottom (center line).||Nothing on the model is left out of the steps.
Check plumb and square||Stand it up. Sight the long edges. If a face racks, find the soft joint and re-join it.||A lean now is a lean forever.

rows.buy: 1×3/4" Plywood 4×8=38.43; 1×#8 x 1-1/4" wood screws=8.47; 1×Wood glue=4.98; 1×GRK RSS #9 x 3-1/8 structural screws=18.97
rows.steps:
Confirm the hang before the first cut||Spice rack. Wall-mounted spice rack 18" wide × 3" deep × 24" high. This hangs on the wall, so the layout marks go on the wall. Find two studs. Typical bottom sits about 48–54" off the floor so jars are at counter height. 9 parts on this list.||This is a wall spice rack, not a floor box. If a number disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). 1 Left upright 24 × 3 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 24 × 3 × 3/4". 3 shelves 16 1/2 × 2 1/4 × 3/4". 3 Jar lips 16 1/2 × 1 1/4 × 3/4". 1 A Back 24 × 16 1/2 × 3/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Stand the rack||B Left upright — 24 × 3 × 3/4"; B Right upright — 24 × 3 × 3/4". A Back — 24 × 16 1/2 × 3/4". D Shelf 1 — 16 1/2 × 2 1/4 × 3/4"; D Shelf 2 — 16 1/2 × 2 1/4 × 3/4"; D Shelf 3 — 16 1/2 × 2 1/4 × 3/4". Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into each D shelf at those marked heights. Use fixed shelves here, screwed in place — jars are heavy and the lips need a solid shelf. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Lay the Left upright, Right upright, Shelf 1 and Back flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the rest fastens to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: Tops of the D shelves sit 3/4", 11 3/4" and 22 3/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 11" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both B uprights before you set any shelf. Front edge flush with the front of both B uprights. Drive 13 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first rack.
Set the shelves||Fasten the D Shelf 2 and Shelf 3 to both B uprights. Fasten each one with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Each layer goes on after the parts it rests on.
Glue the jar lips||C Jar lip 1 — 16 1/2 × 1 1/4 × 3/4"; C Jar lip 2 — 16 1/2 × 1 1/4 × 3/4"; C Jar lip 3 — 16 1/2 × 1 1/4 × 3/4". Glue a 1 1/4" jar lip on the front of every shelf so jars stay on. #8 × 1 1/4" screws from behind the lip into the shelf front edge. Where: Top edges of the C jar lips sit 2", 13" and 24" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 11" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on both B uprights before you fix any jar lip. Front face flush with the front of both B uprights. Drive 21 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 48 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||The lip stands on the front edge of the D shelf. Wipe squeeze-out before it skins.
Hang it on studs||Find two studs. Predrill the A back. Drive 3" structural screws through the A back into the studs — 4 screws. Loaded spice jars will rip off drywall anchors.||Guidance only — hit a stud. Confirm the hang height so jars sit at counter height.

rows.steps:
Confirm the hang before the first cut||Spice rack. Wall-mounted spice rack 36" wide × 4" deep × 24" high. This hangs on the wall, so the layout marks go on the wall. Find two studs. Typical bottom sits about 48–54" off the floor so jars are at counter height. 9 parts on this list. Assumed 36" wide (default size) — type a width to lock it. Assumed 4" deep (default size) — type a depth to lock it.||This is a wall spice rack, not a floor box. If a number disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). 1 Left upright 24 × 4 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 24 × 4 × 3/4". 3 shelves 34 1/2 × 3 1/4 × 3/4". 3 Jar lips 34 1/2 × 1 1/4 × 3/4". 1 A Back 34 1/2 × 24 × 3/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Stand the rack||D Left upright — 24 × 4 × 3/4"; D Right upright — 24 × 4 × 3/4". A Back — 34 1/2 × 24 × 3/4". C Shelf 1 — 34 1/2 × 3 1/4 × 3/4"; C Shelf 2 — 34 1/2 × 3 1/4 × 3/4"; C Shelf 3 — 34 1/2 × 3 1/4 × 3/4". Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into each C shelf at those marked heights. Use fixed shelves here, screwed in place — jars are heavy and the lips need a solid shelf. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Lay the Left upright, Right upright, Shelf 1 and Back flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the rest fastens to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: Tops of the C shelves sit 3/4", 11 3/4" and 22 3/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 11" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both D uprights before you set any shelf. Front edge flush with the front of both D uprights. Drive 15 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first rack.
Set the shelves||Fasten the C Shelf 2 and Shelf 3 to both D uprights. Fasten each one with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Drive 18 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Each layer goes on after the parts it rests on.
Glue the jar lips||B Jar lip 1 — 34 1/2 × 1 1/4 × 3/4"; B Jar lip 2 — 34 1/2 × 1 1/4 × 3/4"; B Jar lip 3 — 34 1/2 × 1 1/4 × 3/4". Glue a 1 1/4" jar lip on the front of every shelf so jars stay on. #8 × 1 1/4" screws from behind the lip into the shelf front edge. Where: Top edges of the B jar lips sit 2", 13" and 24" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 11" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on both D uprights before you fix any jar lip. Front face flush with the front of both D uprights. Drive 27 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 60 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||The lip stands on the front edge of the C shelf. Wipe squeeze-out before it skins.
Hang it on studs||Find two studs. Predrill the A back. Drive 3" structural screws through the A back into the studs — 4 screws. Loaded spice jars will rip off drywall anchors.||Guidance only — hit a stud. Confirm the hang height so jars sit at counter height.

Mark studs across the 24" span. Each shelf rides its own wall cleat screwed into studs. Assumed 24" wide (default size) — type a width to lock it. Assumed 12" tall (default size) — type a height to lock it. Assumed 6" deep (default size) — type a depth to lock it.||If a number on this plan disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Cut the shelves and wall cleats||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). 1 C Wall cleat 24 × 2 1/2 × 3/4". 1 B Shelf 24 × 5 1/4 × 3/4". 1 A Back 24 × 12 × 3/4". B Shelf — 24 × 5 1/4 × 3/4". C Wall cleat — 24 × 2 1/2 × 3/4" Label the waste face.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Set the Shelf backstop||Lay the Shelf backstop flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the next parts fasten to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: Set it on the top of C; overhang 4 1/2" past the front (rear edge flush).||This part was on the model and not yet in a step.
Screw each wall cleat into studs||C Wall cleat — 24 × 2 1/2 × 3/4". Level a cleat on the wall at each marked shelf height, hit at least two studs, and drive 3" structural screws through the cleat into the studs, 2 per stud. Repeat for every marked height (4 in all). Where: Top edge of C Wall cleat sits 2 1/2" up from the bottom edge of the unit.||Guidance only — hit a stud. Drywall anchors will not hold a loaded shelf.
Sit each shelf on its cleat and screw down||B Shelf — 24 × 5 1/4 × 3/4". Marked height: B Shelf at 2½" from the bottom. Set each B shelf on its cleat at the marked height so the back edge is flush to the wall. Drive #8 × 1 1/4" screws down through the B shelf into the cleat.||Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Wipe squeeze-out if you add glue.

rows.steps:
Read this Towel rack 36" × 30" × 12" before you cut||26 pieces of 3/4" Schedule 40 PVC Pipe. Same Towel rack 36" × 30" × 12", every face in that stock. About 36" × 30" × 12".||The cut list has every length. Nothing is left off.
Lay out the footprint on the bench||Tape a rectangle 36" × 12" on the bench. Mark centerlines both ways. The faces go up from this outline.||A square base keeps every later part true.
Cut every marked length||PVC cutter or a fine hacksaw. Deburr so each end seats in the fitting. The cut list is the full list — same letter is the same cut. 26 pieces: 8 × 34 3/8", 4 × 15 1/8", 4 × 14 3/8", 4 × 11", 2 × 3 3/4", 4 × 3 5/8".||A ragged end will not bottom out in a slip tee.
Stand the sides — 8 pieces||8 pieces: 4 × 15 1/8", 4 × 14 3/8". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs.||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Run the rails — 18 pieces||18 pieces: 8 × 34 3/8", 4 × 11", 2 × 3 3/4", 4 × 3 5/8". Solvent cement. Twist a quarter turn and hold until it grabs.||Dry-fit the face, then join.
Check plumb and square||Stand it up. Sight the long edges. If a face racks, find the soft joint and re-join it.||A lean now is a lean forever.

rows.steps:
Confirm the hang before the first cut||Wine rack. Wall-mounted wine rack 24" wide × 12" deep × 14 1/4" high. Holds 12 bottles — 3 rows × 4 across, one opening per bottle (rows on a 4 1/2" pitch, one bottle high). Built 14 1/4" tall — just the rows the bottles need. This hangs on the wall, so the layout marks go on the wall. Find two studs. Typical bottom sits about 36–42" off the floor, or sit it on a counter and still screw it into the studs with 3" structural screws so it stays upright. 13 parts on this list. Assumed 24" wide (default size) — type a width to lock it. Assumed 14 1/4" tall (default size) — type a height to lock it. Assumed 12" deep (default size) — type a depth to lock it.||This is a wine rack, not a bookcase. Bottles lie on their sides. If a number disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). 1 Left upright 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". 2 shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 3 Bottle rails 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". 2 Grid shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 3 Dividers 12 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". 1 A Back 22 1/2 × 14 1/4 × 3/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Stand the rack||E Left upright — 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4"; E Right upright — 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". A Back — 22 1/2 × 14 1/4 × 3/4". D Shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; D Shelf 4 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into every shelf at those marked heights. Then screw the bottom shelf and the shelf above the bottle rows into the divider ends, and the A back onto the shelf edges. Use fixed shelves here, screwed in place — a row of bottles is heavy. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Lay the Left upright flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the next parts fasten to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: Tops of the D shelves sit 3/4" and 14 1/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 13 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both E uprights before you set any shelf. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. rows.steps:
Confirm the footprint before the first cut||Shoe rack. Unit 36" wide × 12" deep × 18" high. Freestanding rectangle. Mark the footprint on the floor. Check it is square. 8 parts on this list. Assumed 36" wide (shoe rack class default) — type a width to lock it. Assumed 18" tall (shoe rack class default) — type a height to lock it. Assumed 12" deep (shoe rack class default) — type a depth to lock it.||If a number on this plan disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list. Geometry is from the bench, not from the prompt's adjectives.
Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8 and 1/4" plywood (backer)||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). From the 3/4" Plywood 4×8: 1 Left upright 18 × 12 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 18 × 12 × 3/4". 1 B Bottom 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". 1 C Shoe shelf 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". 1 D Top 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". 2 Cubby dividers 16 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". From the 1/4" plywood (backer): 1 A Back 34 1/2 × 18 × 1/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Stand the main box||Lay the two E uprights on edge. E Left upright — 18 × 12 × 3/4"; E Right upright — 18 × 12 × 3/4". One join: attach B Bottom to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Where: Top of B Bottom sits 3/4" up from the floor — flush with the bottom ends of both E uprights. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. In all, this step drives 24 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws, from the model's joints.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Attach D Top to both E uprights||One join: attach D Top to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Where: Top of D Top sits 18" up from the floor — flush with the top ends of both E uprights. Its underside rests on the top of both F cubby dividers, 17 1/4" up from the floor. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. These screws are counted in another step's total.||One join at a time — dry-fit, then glue and drive the screws for this join only.
Set cubby dividers||F Cubby divider 1 — 16 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4"; F Cubby divider 2 — 16 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". Space them evenly. Screw through the D top, bottom, and back into each divider. Where: F Cubby divider 1 stands 10 7/8" from the inside face of E Left upright and 11 1/4" from F Cubby divider 2. Square a pencil line across B Bottom at each mark and stand the divider on it. F Cubby divider 2 stands 11 1/4" from F Cubby divider 1 and 10 7/8" from the inside face of E Right upright. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||
Attach A Back to the back of the box||One join: attach A Back to the back edges of both E Uprights, B Bottom and D Top and both F Cubby dividers with 22 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws, one about every 8" along each edge. Square the box first: both diagonals measure the same. Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. These screws are counted in another step's total.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Glue 1 fixed shelf||C Shoe shelf — 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into each shelf at those marked heights. Square every bay. The back is already on and square: slide each shelf in to touch it, then drive 5 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws through A Back into the shelf back edges, one about every 8". These shelves are fixed — no pins. Where: Top of C Shoe shelf sits 8 5/8" up from the top of B Bottom (9 3/8" from the floor). Mark 8 5/8" up from the top of B Bottom on the inside face of both E uprights and line the top face up with the marks. Or cut a spacer block 7 7/8" long, stand it on B Bottom, and rest the part on it while you fasten it. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Drive 13 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 51 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Wipe squeeze-out.
Level it||Level the unit. The A back is already on it so the box stays square. If it sits on a floor that is out, shim the feet, keeping the main box square.||Guidance only — confirm the real footprint before you cut. Not stamped engineering.
Paint it white||Sand every face to 180 grit and wipe off the dust. Brush on a thin coat of Rust-Oleum Painter's Touch Ultra Cover paint, Semi-Gloss White, let it dry 2 hours, sand lightly with 220 grit, then brush on the second coat.||

rows.steps:
Confirm the hang before the first cut||Wine rack. Wall-mounted wine rack 24" wide × 12" deep × 36" high. Holds about 42 bottles — 7 rows of about 6 bottles each, lying side by side on open shelves (rows on a 4 1/2" pitch, one bottle high). The bottle rows sit on a 3 3/4" plinth, recessed like a kick strip, so the top cap lands at the full 36" height. This hangs on the wall, so the layout marks go on the wall. Find two studs. Typical bottom sits about 36–42" off the floor, or sit it on a counter and still screw it into the studs with 3" structural screws so it stays upright. 19 parts on this list. Assumed 24" wide (default size) — type a width to lock it. Assumed 36" tall (default size) — type a height to lock it. Assumed 12" deep (default size) — type a depth to lock it.||This is a wine rack, not a bookcase. Bottles lie on their sides. If a number disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). 1 Left upright 36 × 12 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 36 × 12 × 3/4". 1 D Plinth 22 1/2 × 3 3/4 × 3/4". 8 shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 7 Bottle rails 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". 1 A Back 36 × 22 1/2 × 3/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Set the Plinth||Lay the Plinth flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the next parts fasten to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: Top edge of D Plinth sits 3 3/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. Front face set back 3 1/2" from the front of both B uprights.||This part was on the model and not yet in a step.
Stand the rack||B Left upright — 36 × 12 × 3/4"; B Right upright — 36 × 12 × 3/4". A Back — 36 × 22 1/2 × 3/4". E Shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 2 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 3 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 4 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 5 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 6 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 7 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Shelf 8 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Marked heights: E Shelf 1 at 3 3/4" from the bottom; E Shelf 2 at 8 1/4" from the bottom; E Shelf 3 at 12 3/4" from the bottom; E Shelf 4 at 17 1/4" from the bottom; E Shelf 5 at 21 3/4" from the bottom; E Shelf 6 at 26 1/4" from the bottom; E Shelf 7 at 30 3/4" from the bottom; E Shelf 8 at 35 1/4" from the bottom. Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into each E shelf at those marked heights. Use fixed shelves here, screwed in place — a row of bottles is heavy. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Lay the Left upright, Right upright and Back flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the rest fastens to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first rack.
Set the shelves||Fasten the E Shelf 1, Shelf 2, Shelf 3, Shelf 4, Shelf 5, Shelf 6, Shelf 7 and Shelf 8 to both B uprights. Fasten each one with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Tops of the E shelves sit 4 1/2", 9", 13 1/2", 18", 22 1/2", 27", 31 1/2" and 36" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 4 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both B uprights before you set any shelf. Or cut a spacer block 3 3/4" long, stand it on the bottom edge, and rest the lowest shelf on it. rows.steps:
Confirm the hang before the first cut||Wine rack. Wall-mounted wine rack 24" wide × 12" deep × 14 1/4" high. Holds 12 bottles — 3 rows × 4 across, one opening per bottle (rows on a 4 1/2" pitch, one bottle high). Built 14 1/4" tall — just the rows the bottles need. This hangs on the wall, so the layout marks go on the wall. Find two studs. Typical bottom sits about 36–42" off the floor, or sit it on a counter and still screw it into the studs with 3" structural screws so it stays upright. 13 parts on this list. Assumed 24" wide (default size) — type a width to lock it. Assumed 14 1/4" tall (default size) — type a height to lock it.||This is a wine rack, not a bookcase. Bottles lie on their sides. If a number disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). 1 Left upright 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". 2 shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 3 Bottle rails 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". 2 Grid shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 3 Dividers 12 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". 1 A Back 22 1/2 × 14 1/4 × 3/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Stand the rack||E Left upright — 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4"; E Right upright — 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". A Back — 22 1/2 × 14 1/4 × 3/4". D Shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; D Shelf 4 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into every shelf at those marked heights. Then screw the bottom shelf and the shelf above the bottle rows into the divider ends, and the A back onto the shelf edges. Use fixed shelves here, screwed in place — a row of bottles is heavy. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Lay the Left upright flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the next parts fasten to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: Tops of the D shelves sit 3/4" and 14 1/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 13 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both E uprights before you set any shelf. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Tops of the C grid shelves sit 5 1/4" and 9 3/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 4 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both E uprights before you set any grid shelf. Or cut a spacer block 4 1/2" long, stand it on the bottom edge, and rest the lowest grid shelf on it. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Drive 18 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Every opening should take a bottle with room to spare.
Notch and slot the bottle grid||. C Grid shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; C Grid shelf 2 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Dividers: cut 2 notches 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the front edge, one where each shelf crosses, at 3 3/4" and 8 1/4" up from the bottom end. Middle shelves: cut 3 notches 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the back edge, one at each divider crossing, at 5 1/16", 10 7/8" and 16 11/16" from the left end. Saw both sides of each notch and chisel out the waste. Slot every divider down over the middle shelves so the front edges line up — an egg-crate grid. Dry-fit, then glue the laps. Fasten the C Grid shelf 1 to both E uprights with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Cut one notch, test it on a scrap of the same board, then cut the rest. A snug hand-press fit is right — no hammering.
Glue the bottle rails||B Bottle rail 1 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; B Bottle rail 2 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; B Bottle rail 3 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". Glue a 1 1/2" rail on the front of every shelf that carries a row of bottles so they stay on. #8 × 1 1/4" screws from behind the rail into the shelf front edge. Drive 21 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||The rail stands on the front edge of the shelf. Wipe squeeze-out before it skins. Bottles lie on their sides, necks facing out.
Set the Bottle divider 1, Bottle divider 2 and Bottle divider 3||Set the Bottle divider 1 on the Shelf 1 and the B Bottle rail 1. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Set the Bottle divider 2 on the Shelf 1 and the B Bottle rail 1. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Set the Bottle divider 3 on the Shelf 1 and the B Bottle rail 1. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Center F Bottle divider 1: 5 1/16" from the inside face of E Left upright and 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 2. Square a pencil line across D Shelf 1 at each mark and stand the divider on it. Center F Bottle divider 2: 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 1 and 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 3. Center F Bottle divider 3: 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 2 and 5 1/16" from the inside face of E Right upright. Drive 48 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 101 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||It goes on once every part under it is in place.
Hang it on studs||Find two studs. Predrill the A back. Drive 3" structural screws through the A back into the studs — 4 to 6 screws. A loaded wine rack will rip off drywall anchors.||Guidance only — hit a stud. Confirm the hang height so you can reach a bottle.

rows.steps:
Confirm the hang before the first cut||Wine rack. Wall-mounted wine rack 12" wide × 12" deep × 30" high. Holds 12 bottles at this height — 8 short of the 20 you asked for; about 45 3/4" tall fits all 20 (or about 23 1/4" wide at 30" tall). 6 rows × 2 across, one opening per bottle (rows on a 4 1/2" pitch, one bottle high), inside the 30" height you typed. The bottle rows sit on a 2 1/4" plinth, recessed like a kick strip, so the top cap lands at the 30" height you typed. This hangs on the wall, so the layout marks go on the wall. Find two studs. Typical bottom sits about 36–42" off the floor, or sit it on a counter and still screw it into the studs with 3" structural screws so it stays upright. 18 parts on this list.||This is a wine rack, not a bookcase. Bottles lie on their sides. If a number disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). 1 Left upright 30 × 12 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 30 × 12 × 3/4". 1 G Plinth 10 1/2 × 2 1/4 × 3/4". 2 shelves 11 1/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". 6 Bottle rails 10 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". 5 Grid shelves 11 1/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". 1 C Divider 26 1/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". 1 A Back 30 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Stand the rack||B Left upright — 30 × 12 × 3/4"; B Right upright — 30 × 12 × 3/4". A Back — 30 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". E Shelf 1 — 11 1/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4"; E Shelf 7 — 11 1/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into every shelf at those marked heights. Then screw the bottom shelf and the shelf above the bottle rows into the divider ends, and the A back onto the shelf edges. G Plinth — 10 1/2 × 2 1/4 × 3/4": glue and screw the G plinth between the uprights under the bottom shelf, recessed 3 1/2" from the front — the recessed base keeps the front clean and lifts the rows so the top cap lands at the full height. Use fixed shelves here, screwed in place — a row of bottles is heavy. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Lay the Left upright, Right upright, Plinth and Back flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the rest fastens to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: Top edge of G Plinth sits 2 1/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. Front face set back 3 1/2" from the front of both B uprights. Drive 12 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Every opening should take a bottle with room to spare.
Notch and slot the bottle grid||C Bottle divider 1 — 26 1/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". D Grid shelf 1 — 11 1/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4"; D Grid shelf 2 — 11 1/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4"; D Grid shelf 3 — 11 1/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4"; D Grid shelf 4 — 11 1/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4"; D Grid shelf 5 — 11 1/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". Dividers: cut 5 notches 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the front edge, one where each shelf crosses, at 3 3/4", 8 1/4", 12 3/4", 17 1/4" and 21 3/4" up from the bottom end. Middle shelves: cut a notch 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the back edge, one at each divider crossing, at 4 7/8" from the left end. Saw both sides of each notch and chisel out the waste. Slot every divider down over the middle shelves so the front edges line up — an egg-crate grid. Dry-fit, then glue the laps. Fasten the D Grid shelf 1, Grid shelf 2, Grid shelf 3, Grid shelf 4 and Grid shelf 5 to both B uprights. Fasten each one with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Tops of the D grid shelves sit 7 1/2", 12", 16 1/2", 21" and 25 1/2" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 4 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both B uprights before you set any grid shelf. Or cut a spacer block 6 3/4" long, stand it on the bottom edge, and rest the lowest grid shelf on it. Front edge flush with the front of both B uprights. Drive 30 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Cut one notch, test it on a scrap of the same board, then cut the rest. A snug hand-press fit is right — no hammering.
Set the shelves||Fasten the Shelf 1 and Shelf 7 to both B uprights. Fasten each one with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Tops of the E shelves sit 3" and 30" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 27" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both B uprights before you set any shelf. Or cut a spacer block 2 1/4" long, stand it on the bottom edge, and rest the lowest shelf on it. Front edge flush with the front of both B uprights. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Each layer goes on after the parts it rests on.
Glue the bottle rails||F Bottle rail 1 — 10 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; F Bottle rail 2 — 10 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; F Bottle rail 3 — 10 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; F Bottle rail 4 — 10 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; F Bottle rail 5 — 10 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; F Bottle rail 6 — 10 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". Glue a 1 1/2" rail on the front of every shelf that carries a row of bottles so they stay on. #8 × 1 1/4" screws from behind the rail into the shelf front edge. Drive 36 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||The rail stands on the front edge of the shelf. Wipe squeeze-out before it skins. Bottles lie on their sides, necks facing out.
Set the bottle dividers||Set the Bottle divider 1 on the Shelf 1 and the F Bottle rail 1. Fasten each one with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Center C Divider: 4 7/8" from the inside face of B Left upright and 4 7/8" from the inside face of B Right upright. Square a pencil line across E Shelf 1 at each mark and stand the divider on it. Drive 30 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 122 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||Each layer goes on after the parts it rests on.
Hang it on studs||Find two studs. Predrill the A back. Drive 3" structural screws through the A back into the studs — 4 to 6 screws. A loaded wine rack will rip off drywall anchors.||Guidance only — hit a stud. Confirm the hang height so you can reach a bottle.

rows.steps:
Confirm the hang before the first cut||Wine rack. Wall-mounted wine rack 24" wide × 12" deep × 36" high. Holds 35 bottles (room for the 12 bottles you asked for; 7 rows × 5 across, one opening per bottle, rows on a 4 1/2" pitch, one bottle high). The bottle rows sit on a 3 3/4" plinth, recessed like a kick strip, so the top cap lands at the 36" height you typed. This hangs on the wall, so the layout marks go on the wall. Find two studs. Typical bottom sits about 36–42" off the floor, or sit it on a counter and still screw it into the studs with 3" structural screws so it stays upright. 23 parts on this list.||This is a wine rack, not a bookcase. Bottles lie on their sides. If a number disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). 1 Left upright 36 × 12 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 36 × 12 × 3/4". 1 F Plinth 22 1/2 × 3 3/4 × 3/4". 2 shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 7 Bottle rails 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". 6 Grid shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 4 Dividers 30 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". 1 A Back 36 × 22 1/2 × 3/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Stand the rack||B Left upright — 36 × 12 × 3/4"; B Right upright — 36 × 12 × 3/4". A Back — 36 × 22 1/2 × 3/4". G Shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; G Shelf 8 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into every shelf at those marked heights. Then screw the bottom shelf and the shelf above the bottle rows into the divider ends, and the A back onto the shelf edges. F Plinth — 22 1/2 × 3 3/4 × 3/4": glue and screw the F plinth between the uprights under the bottom shelf, recessed 3 1/2" from the front — the recessed base keeps the front clean and lifts the rows so the top cap lands at the full height. Use fixed shelves here, screwed in place — a row of bottles is heavy. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Lay the Left upright, Right upright, Plinth and Back flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the rest fastens to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: Top edge of F Plinth sits 3 3/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. Front face set back 3 1/2" from the front of both B uprights. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Every opening should take a bottle with room to spare.
Notch and slot the bottle grid||C Bottle divider 1 — 30 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4"; C Bottle divider 2 — 30 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4"; C Bottle divider 3 — 30 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4"; C Bottle divider 4 — 30 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". E Grid shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Grid shelf 2 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Grid shelf 3 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Grid shelf 4 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Grid shelf 5 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; E Grid shelf 6 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Dividers: cut 6 notches 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the front edge, one where each shelf crosses, at 3 3/4", 8 1/4", 12 3/4", 17 1/4", 21 3/4" and 26 1/4" up from the bottom end. Middle shelves: cut 4 notches 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the back edge, one at each divider crossing, at 3 7/8", 8 9/16", 13 3/16" and 17 7/8" from the left end. Saw both sides of each notch and chisel out the waste. Slot every divider down over the middle shelves so the front edges line up — an egg-crate grid. Dry-fit, then glue the laps. Fasten the E Grid shelf 1, Grid shelf 2, Grid shelf 3, Grid shelf 4, Grid shelf 5 and Grid shelf 6 to both B uprights. Fasten each one with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Tops of the E grid shelves sit 9", 13 1/2", 18", 22 1/2", 27" and 31 1/2" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 4 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both B uprights before you set any grid shelf. Or cut a spacer block 8 1/4" long, stand it on the bottom edge, and rest the lowest grid shelf on it. Front edge flush with the front of both B uprights. Drive 42 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Cut one notch, test it on a scrap of the same board, then cut the rest. A snug hand-press fit is right — no hammering.
Set the shelves||Fasten the Shelf 1 and Shelf 8 to both B uprights. Fasten each one with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Tops of the G shelves sit 4 1/2" and 36" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 31 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both B uprights before you set any shelf. Or cut a spacer block 3 3/4" long, stand it on the bottom edge, and rest the lowest shelf on it. Front edge flush with the front of both B uprights. Drive 17 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Each layer goes on after the parts it rests on.
Glue the bottle rails||D Bottle rail 1 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; D Bottle rail 2 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; D Bottle rail 3 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; D Bottle rail 4 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; D Bottle rail 5 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; D Bottle rail 6 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; D Bottle rail 7 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". Glue a 1 1/2" rail on the front of every shelf that carries a row of bottles so they stay on. #8 × 1 1/4" screws from behind the rail into the shelf front edge. Drive 49 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||The rail stands on the front edge of the shelf. Wipe squeeze-out before it skins. Bottles lie on their sides, necks facing out.
Set the bottle dividers||Set the Bottle divider 1, Bottle divider 2, Bottle divider 3 and Bottle divider 4 on the Shelf 1 and the D Bottle rail 1. Fasten each one with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Center C Bottle divider 1: 3 7/8" from the inside face of B Left upright and 3 7/8" from C Bottle divider 2. Square a pencil line across G Shelf 1 at each mark and stand the divider on it. Center C Bottle divider 2: 3 7/8" from C Bottle divider 1 and 3 7/8" from C Bottle divider 3. Center C Bottle divider 3: 3 7/8" from C Bottle divider 2 and 3 7/8" from C Bottle divider 4. Center C Bottle divider 4: 3 7/8" from C Bottle divider 3 and 3 7/8" from the inside face of B Right upright. Drive 136 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 258 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||Each layer goes on after the parts it rests on.
Hang it on studs||Find two studs. Predrill the A back. Drive 3" structural screws through the A back into the studs — 4 to 6 screws. A loaded wine rack will rip off drywall anchors.||Guidance only — hit a stud. Confirm the hang height so you can reach a bottle.

rows.steps:
Confirm the hang before the first cut||Wine rack. Wall-mounted wine rack 24" wide × 12" deep × 14 1/4" high. Holds 12 bottles — 3 rows × 4 across, one opening per bottle (rows on a 4 1/2" pitch, one bottle high). Built 14 1/4" tall — just the rows the bottles need. This hangs on the wall, so the layout marks go on the wall. Find two studs. Typical bottom sits about 36–42" off the floor, or sit it on a counter and still screw it into the studs with 3" structural screws so it stays upright. 13 parts on this list. Assumed 24" wide (default size) — type a width to lock it. Assumed 14 1/4" tall (default size) — type a height to lock it.||This is a wine rack, not a bookcase. Bottles lie on their sides. If a number disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). 1 Left upright 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". 2 shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 3 Bottle rails 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". 2 Grid shelves 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". 3 Dividers 12 3/4 × 10 1/2 × 3/4". 1 A Back 22 1/2 × 14 1/4 × 3/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Stand the rack||E Left upright — 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4"; E Right upright — 14 1/4 × 12 × 3/4". A Back — 22 1/2 × 14 1/4 × 3/4". D Shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; D Shelf 4 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into every shelf at those marked heights. Then screw the bottom shelf and the shelf above the bottle rows into the divider ends, and the A back onto the shelf edges. Use fixed shelves here, screwed in place — a row of bottles is heavy. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Lay the Left upright flat on the bench, square to the marks: the base the next parts fasten to. The finished piece goes on the wall once it is built. Where: Tops of the D shelves sit 3/4" and 14 1/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 13 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both E uprights before you set any shelf. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Tops of the C grid shelves sit 5 1/4" and 9 3/4" up from the bottom edge of the unit. That is 4 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both E uprights before you set any grid shelf. Or cut a spacer block 4 1/2" long, stand it on the bottom edge, and rest the lowest grid shelf on it. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Drive 18 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Every opening should take a bottle with room to spare.
Notch and slot the bottle grid||. C Grid shelf 1 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4"; C Grid shelf 2 — 22 1/2 × 11 1/4 × 3/4". Dividers: cut 2 notches 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the front edge, one where each shelf crosses, at 3 3/4" and 8 1/4" up from the bottom end. Middle shelves: cut 3 notches 3/4" wide × 5 1/4" deep from the back edge, one at each divider crossing, at 5 1/16", 10 7/8" and 16 11/16" from the left end. Saw both sides of each notch and chisel out the waste. Slot every divider down over the middle shelves so the front edges line up — an egg-crate grid. Dry-fit, then glue the laps. Fasten the C Grid shelf 1 to both E uprights with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||Cut one notch, test it on a scrap of the same board, then cut the rest. A snug hand-press fit is right — no hammering.
Glue the bottle rails||B Bottle rail 1 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; B Bottle rail 2 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4"; B Bottle rail 3 — 22 1/2 × 1 1/2 × 3/4". Glue a 1 1/2" rail on the front of every shelf that carries a row of bottles so they stay on. #8 × 1 1/4" screws from behind the rail into the shelf front edge. Drive 21 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||The rail stands on the front edge of the shelf. Wipe squeeze-out before it skins. Bottles lie on their sides, necks facing out.
Set the Bottle divider 1, Bottle divider 2 and Bottle divider 3||Set the Bottle divider 1 on the Shelf 1 and the B Bottle rail 1. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Set the Bottle divider 2 on the Shelf 1 and the B Bottle rail 1. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Set the Bottle divider 3 on the Shelf 1 and the B Bottle rail 1. Fasten it with #8 × 1 1/4" screws, the same screws on the Buy list. Where: Center F Bottle divider 1: 5 1/16" from the inside face of E Left upright and 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 2. Square a pencil line across D Shelf 1 at each mark and stand the divider on it. Center F Bottle divider 2: 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 1 and 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 3. Center F Bottle divider 3: 5 1/16" from F Bottle divider 2 and 5 1/16" from the inside face of E Right upright. Drive 48 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 101 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||It goes on once every part under it is in place.
Hang it on studs||Find two studs. Predrill the A back. Drive 3" structural screws through the A back into the studs — 4 to 6 screws. A loaded wine rack will rip off drywall anchors.||Guidance only — hit a stud. Confirm the hang height so you can reach a bottle.

Geometry is from the bench, not from the prompt's adjectives.
Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8 and 1/4" plywood (backer)||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). From the 3/4" Plywood 4×8: 1 Left upright 18 × 12 × 3/4". 1 Right upright 18 × 12 × 3/4". 1 B Bottom 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". 1 C Shoe shelf 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". 1 D Top 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". 2 Cubby dividers 16 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". From the 1/4" plywood (backer): 1 A Back 34 1/2 × 18 × 1/4". Label every piece on the waste face before you move the stack.||Support the offcut so it does not splinter. If a number here disagrees with the cut list, trust the cut list.
Stand the main box||Lay the two E uprights on edge. E Left upright — 18 × 12 × 3/4"; E Right upright — 18 × 12 × 3/4". One join: attach B Bottom to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Where: Top of B Bottom sits 3/4" up from the floor — flush with the bottom ends of both E uprights. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. In all, this step drives 24 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws, from the model's joints.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Attach D Top to both E uprights||One join: attach D Top to both E uprights with 4 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Where: Top of D Top sits 18" up from the floor — flush with the top ends of both E uprights. Its underside rests on the top of both F cubby dividers, 17 1/4" up from the floor. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. These screws are counted in another step's total.||One join at a time — dry-fit, then glue and drive the screws for this join only.
Set cubby dividers||F Cubby divider 1 — 16 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4"; F Cubby divider 2 — 16 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". Space them evenly. Screw through the D top, bottom, and back into each divider. Where: F Cubby divider 1 stands 10 7/8" from the inside face of E Left upright and 11 1/4" from F Cubby divider 2. Square a pencil line across B Bottom at each mark and stand the divider on it. F Cubby divider 2 stands 11 1/4" from F Cubby divider 1 and 10 7/8" from the inside face of E Right upright. Drive 14 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2).||
Attach A Back to the back of the box||One join: attach A Back to the back edges of both E Uprights, B Bottom and D Top and both F Cubby dividers with 22 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws, one about every 8" along each edge. These screws are counted in another step's total.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Glue 1 fixed shelf||C Shoe shelf — 34 1/2 × 11 3/4 × 3/4". Glue and #8 × 1 1/4" screws through the uprights into each shelf at those marked heights. Square every bay. The back is already on and square: slide each shelf in to touch it, then drive 5 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws through A Back into the shelf back edges, one about every 8". These shelves are fixed — no pins. Where: Top of C Shoe shelf sits 8 5/8" up from the top of B Bottom (9 3/8" from the floor). Mark 8 5/8" up from the top of B Bottom on the inside face of both E uprights and line the top face up with the marks. Or cut a spacer block 7 7/8" long, stand it on B Bottom, and rest the part on it while you fasten it. Front edge flush with the front of both E uprights. Drive 13 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 51 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Wipe squeeze-out.
Level it||Level the unit. The A back is already on it so the box stays square. If it sits on a floor that is out, shim the feet, keeping the main box square.||Guidance only — confirm the real footprint before you cut. Not stamped engineering.

Cut the 3/4" Plywood 4×8 and 1/4" plywood (backer)||Circular saw and a straightedge — or take this cut list to the lumber aisle and have them cut the sheets. Good face up. Write the letter from the cut list on the waste face (the side nobody sees). Stand the main box||Lay the two B uprights on edge. B Left upright — 78 × 16 × 3/4"; B Right upright — 78 × 16 × 3/4". One join: attach D Bottom to both B uprights with 4 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Attach F Top to both B uprights||One join: attach F Top to both B uprights with 4 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws (2 per upright). Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. Where: Top of F Top sits 78" up from the floor — flush with the top ends of both B uprights. Front edge flush with the front of both B uprights. These screws are counted in another step's total.||One join at a time — dry-fit, then glue and drive the screws for this join only.
Attach A Back to the back of the box||One join: attach A Back to the back edges of both B Uprights, F Top and D Bottom with 28 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws, one about every 8" along each edge. Square the box first: both diagonals measure the same. Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. These screws are counted in another step's total.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. A 1/8" difference will show in the doors. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Pin 4 adjustable shelves — 4 pins each||E Shelf 1 — 30 × 15 1/2 × 3/4"; E Shelf 2 — 30 × 15 1/2 × 3/4"; E Shelf 3 — 30 × 15 1/2 × 3/4"; E Shelf 4 — 30 × 15 1/2 × 3/4". Drill 13/64" pin holes (a snug fit for 3/16" pins) in both B uprights (and dividers if the bay is split) at those marked heights, 1¼" from the front, 1¼" apart — the standard shelf-pin spacing. Four pins per shelf (16 pins total). Leave the shelves loose on the pins so you can move them later. Where: Tops of the E shelves sit 16 1/16", 31 3/8", 46 5/8" and 61 15/16" up from the top of D Bottom (16 13/16", 32 1/8", 47 3/8" and 62 11/16" from the floor). Or cut a spacer block 15 5/16" long, stand it on D Bottom, and rest the lowest shelf on it. Front edge set back 1/8" from the front of both B uprights. Adjustable: those are the default spots — the pins let you set a shelf anywhere between the top of D Bottom (3/4") and the underside of F Top (77 1/4").||A pegboard jig or a shelf-pin jig beats measuring every hole twice.
Hang 2 doors — 4 concealed hinges each||One join per door: hang each C Door with 4 concealed hinges. C Left door — 77 7/8 × 15 5/8 × 3/4"; C Right door — 77 7/8 × 15 5/8 × 3/4". Four concealed hinges per door (8 hinges total). Leave a 1/16" gap all round and 1/8" between doors. Overlay the main box (the C door sits on top of the face, not inside the opening). Soft-close if you bought them. Adjust the screws until the gap is even. Screw one bar pull centered on each C door. Open and close each C door — gaps even. Where: Hinge centers 3" down from the top and 3" up from the bottom of each C door (71 7/8" apart), with 2 more evenly between at 26 15/16" and 50 15/16" up from the door's bottom edge, on each door's hinge edge — on the cabinet side that is 3 1/16", 27", 51" and 74 15/16" up from the floor. Pull on the edge opposite the hinges of each 15 5/8" × 77 7/8" door: centered 1 1/8" in from that edge and 38 15/16" down from the top edge.||
Level it||Level the unit. The A back is already on it so the box stays square. If it sits on a floor that is out, shim the feet, keeping the main box square.||Guidance only — confirm the real footprint before you cut. Not stamped engineering.

Cut list has two ¾" plies — glue them face-to-face (laminate) so the finished work surface is 1½" thick, then glue and screw the stack down into the uprights and the knee dividers. Front edge flush. Iron-on edge banding (thin veneer strip that covers the raw plywood edge) on the front if people will see it. Where: Top of F Counter sits 35 1/2" up from the floor. Its underside rests on the top of both H dividers, 34" up from the floor. Front edge flush with the front of both B uprights. Drive 17 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). Screw through the bottom and the vanity counter into each divider.||
Attach A Back to the back of the box||One join: attach A Back to the back edges of both B Uprights, both H Knee dividers, Vanity counter, E Bottom, F Counter and D Divider with 57 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws, one about every 8" along each edge. Square the box first: both diagonals measure the same. Glue the mating edges. Predrill near the ends so the ply does not split. These screws are counted in another step's total.||Check both diagonals before the glue skins. A 1/8" difference will show in the doors. Dry-fit first (assemble without glue) if this is your first box.
Kick strip on the banks only||Left kick strip — 6 1/2 × 3 1/2 × 3/4"; Right kick strip — 6 1/2 × 3 1/2 × 3/4". The kick strip is the recessed strip at the floor so your toes clear when you stand close. Kick the drawer banks only. Leave the knee open to the floor. Where: Top edges of both T kick strips sit 3 1/2" up from the floor. Front face set back 3 1/2" from the front of both B uprights and both H dividers. Drive 8 × #8 × 1 1/4" screws in this step, from the model's joints: one about every 8" along each joint (at least 2). That brings the build to 95 screws from the model's joints, the count on the Buy list.||
Build 6 drawers (sides, fronts, backs, and bottoms)||From the cut list: two Drawer sides, one N Drawer back, and one Drawer bottom per drawer (6 drawers). Glue and nail each box square. The fronts go on after the boxes are hung, so every gap lines up.||Dry-fit the box in the bay (assemble without glue) before the glue goes on.
Hang 6 drawers on 16" slides||One pair of 16" side-mount slides per drawer (metal tracks that screw to the sides of the box and the cabinet). Slide length = box depth. Hang the slides on the dividers first, then set the boxes. Confirm the slide against the 17" main box before you buy. Where: Slide center lines (the middle of each drawer box's height): 7 11/16", 16 7/8" and 27 7/8" up from the floor — the same in every bank. Mark every line on B and H before you hang any slide, and keep each slide's front end on the line.||A 16" box takes a 16" slide. 6 pairs of 16" slides total.
Fit 6 drawer fronts (false fronts)||Each O Drawer front is a false front — the show face screwed onto the front of its box, standing proud of the cabinet. With the boxes hung, set each O Drawer front in place and screw it on from inside the box. Edge-band the plywood edge people see (thin veneer strip over the raw edge) if the main box is ply. One cup pull centered on each front. Where: Pull centered on each 7 1/8" × 8 3/8" drawer front: 3 9/16" from each side and 4 3/16" down from the top edge — mark the center with crossed diagonals. Pull centered on each 7 1/8" × 9 5/8" drawer front: 3 9/16" from each side and 4 13/16" down from the top edge — mark the center with crossed diagonals. Pull centered on each 7 1/8" × 12 1/8" drawer front: 3 9/16" from each side and 6 1/16" down from the top edge — mark the center with crossed diagonals. Drawer fronts, the same in every bank: bottom edges 3 1/2", 12 1/16" and 21 13/16" up from the floor, gaps between fronts 3/16" and 1/8" from the bottom up, sides 1/16" in from the centerline of the wall on each side. Hold each front with double-sided tape or clamps, check the gaps, then screw it on from inside the box.||A playing card between neighbouring fronts keeps the 1/8" gaps even while you drive the screws.
Pin 6 adjustable shelves — 4 pins each||I Left linen shelf 1 — 17 7/8 × 16 1/2 × 3/4"; I Right towel shelf 1 — 17 7/8 × 16 1/2 × 3/4"; I Left linen shelf 2 — 17 7/8 × 16 1/2 × 3/4"; I Right towel shelf 2 — 17 7/8 × 16 1/2 × 3/4"; I Left linen shelf 3 — 17 7/8 × 16 1/2 × 3/4"; I Right towel shelf 3 — 17 7/8 × 16 1/2 × 3/4". Drill 13/64" pin holes (a snug fit for 3/16" pins) in both B uprights (and dividers if the bay is split) at those marked heights, 1¼" from the front, 1¼" apart — the standard shelf-pin spacing. Four pins per shelf piece (24 pins total). Leave the shelves loose on the pins so you can move them later. Where: Tops of the I shelves sit 13 7/16", 24 15/16" and 36 1/2" up from the top of E Bottom (68 3/16", 79 11/16" and 91 1/4" from the floor) — the same in each bay. That is 11 1/2" apart, measured top to top. Mark every height on the inside face of both B uprights and D before you set any shelf. Or cut a spacer block 12 11/16" long, stand it on E Bottom, and rest the lowest shelf on it. Front edge set back 1/8" from the front of both B uprights and D. Adjustable: those are the default spots — the pins let you set a shelf anywhere between the top of E Bottom (54 3/4") and the underside of G Top (101 1/4").||A pegboard jig or a shelf-pin jig beats measuring every hole twice.
Hang 2 doors — 3 concealed hinges each||One join per door: hang each door with 3 concealed hinges. Left upper door — 47 7/8 × 18 7/8 × 3/4"; Right upper door — 47 7/8 × 18 7/8 × 3/4". Three concealed hinges per door (6 hinges total). Leave a 1/16" gap all round and 1/8" between doors. Overlay the main box (the door sits on top of the face, not inside the opening). Soft-close if you bought them. Adjust the screws until the gap is even. Screw one bar pull centered on each door. Open and close each door — gaps even. Where: Hinge centers 3" down from the top and 3" up from the bottom of each C door (41 7/8" apart), with the middle hinge at 23 15/16" — halfway, on each door's hinge edge — on the cabinet side that is 57 1/16", 78" and 98 15/16" up from the floor. Pull on the edge opposite the hinges of each 18 7/8" × 47 7/8" door: centered 1 1/8" in from that edge and 23 15/16" down from the top edge.||
Hang the bought mirror||Vanity mirror — 22 × 16 1/2 × 1/4". Buy glass this size; it comes cut to size from a glass shop, apart from the plywood. Hang over the knee, between the F counter and the uppers. French cleat (two interlocking angled strips — one on the wall, one on the mirror) or mirror clips into studs — not into the plywood back alone. Glue the Vanity mirror to the Back (stud-anchored) and clamp it until it sets. It is too thin for a screw. Where: Bottom edge of the vanity mirror sits 36" up from the floor — 1/2" above the top of F Counter. Centered side to side: 7 1/4" from the inside face of B Left upright and of B Right upright.||
Shim, then screw into studs||Fasten the back and both B uprights into the studs you marked. Shim the tight side (thin wedges to fill the gap — R 1 3/4" / L 5 1/8"). Scribe (mark and cut the edge to match the wall) — ease it into place. The rectangle stays a rectangle.||Guidance only — confirm plumbing, studs, and the real opening before you cut. Not stamped engineering.

Read this Big Ben before you cut||385 pieces of Standard Popsicle Stick. 257 marked cuts (1 × 2 5/8", 4 × 2 5/16", 32 × 2 1/8", 15 × 2", 36 × 1 13/16", 33 × 1 5/8", 26 × 1 1/2", 14 × 1 3/8", 43 × 1 5/16", 33 × 1 1/8", 12 × 1", 4 × 7/8", and 1 more lengths — every one is on the cut list). 128 pieces stay full stock. Envelope about 5" × 25" × 5".||Trust the cut list.
Lay out the footprint on the bench||Tape a rectangle 5" × 5" on the bench. Mark centerlines both ways.||A square base keeps every later part true.
Cut the Standard Popsicle Stick||42 A Brace 4 1/2 × 3/8 × 1/16". 12 B Leg 4 1/2 × 3/8 × 1/16". 8 C Tip 4 1/2 × 3/8 × 1/16". 8 D Brace 4 1/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 4 E Leg 4 1/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 1 F Rail 4 × 3/8 × 1/16". 3 G Brace 3 1/2 × 3/8 × 1/16". 1 H Rail 3 3/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 2 I Rail 3 1/4 × 3/8 × 1/16". 4 J Base 3 × 3/8 × 1/16". 3 K Leg 3 × 3/8 × 1/16". 4 L Rail 3 × 3/8 × 1/16". 32 M Ring 3 × 3/8 × 1/16". 4 N Leg 2 7/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 1 O Brace 2 5/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 4 P Leg 2 1/4 × 3/8 × 1/16". 15 Q Brace 2 1/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 9 R Leg 2 1/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 8 S Rail 2 1/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 5 T Brace 2 × 3/8 × 1/16". 8 U Leg 2 × 3/8 × 1/16". 2 V Ring 2 × 3/8 × 1/16". 16 W Brace 1 3/4 × 3/8 × 1/16". 8 X Leg 1 3/4 × 3/8 × 1/16". 12 Y Ring 1 3/4 × 3/8 × 1/16". 4 Z Brace 1 5/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 29 AA Leg 1 5/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 17 AB Brace 1 1/2 × 3/8 × 1/16". 9 AC Leg 1 1/2 × 3/8 × 1/16". 10 AD Brace 1 3/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 4 AE Leg 1 3/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 23 AF Brace 1 1/4 × 3/8 × 1/16". 2 AG Leg 1 1/4 × 3/8 × 1/16". 4 AH Rail 1 1/4 × 3/8 × 1/16". 14 AI Ring 1 1/4 × 3/8 × 1/16". 19 AJ Brace 1 1/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 5 AK Leg 1 1/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 9 AL Rail 1 1/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 11 AM Brace 1 × 3/8 × 1/16". 1 AN Tip 1 × 3/8 × 1/16". 4 AO Brace 7/8 × 3/8 × 1/16". 4 AP Rail 3/4 × 3/8 × 1/16". Snips or a razor on a scrap board. Mark A, B, C on the first of each size, then batch the rest.||One wrong cut wastes a stick. Cut long, then sneak up on the line.
Dry-fit the base, then glue it — 4 bases||4 bases. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. Dry-fit the joint, then join. Everything above sits on this. Set the 4 bases on the floor, square to the marks. It is the base the next parts fasten to. Where: All 4 bases lie flat on the floor (center line).||Everything above sits on this.
Raise the legs, one bay at a time — 101 legs||101 legs. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. Dry-fit the joint, then join. Glue only as high as you can still reach the joints. Set the 101 legs on the floor, square to the marks. It is the base the next parts fasten to. Where: The 51 legs stand plumb, 4 1/2" tall. The 50 slanted legs run from 4 11/16" up to 20 3/16" up — end to end on the joints in the picture.||Glue only as high as you can still reach the joints.
Add the diagonals and web — 178 braces||178 braces. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. Dry-fit the joint, then join. Diagonals kill racking. Set the 178 braces on the floor, square to the marks. It is the base the next parts fasten to. Where: The braces lie at 12 3/4", 13 13/16" and 15 3/8" up from the floor (center lines). The 10 braces stand plumb, 2 1/8" tall. The 147 slanted braces run from the floor to 17 1/4" up — end to end on the joints in the picture.||Diagonals kill racking.
Join the courses — 60 courses||60 courses. Dry-fit each one, then join it where it meets the body. Set the 60 rings on the 101 legs and the 178 braces. Fasten it with glue, the same glue on the Buy list. Where: The rings stack in 11 layers from 1 9/16" to 20 3/16" up from the floor — about 1 7/8" per layer. The 16 slanted rings run from 12 3/4" up to 14 7/8" up — end to end on the joints in the picture.||Every part on the bench is in a step.
Lace the horizontal rails — 33 rails||33 rails. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. Dry-fit the joint, then join. Rails lock the legs. Where: The rails lie at 12 1/2", 12 3/4", 13 13/16", 15 3/8" and 17 1/4" up from the floor (center lines). The 8 slanted rails run from 12 1/2" up to 12 3/4" up — end to end on the joints in the picture.||Rails lock the legs.
Join the tips — 9 tips||9 tips. Dry-fit each one, then join it where it meets the body. Set the 9 tips on the 101 legs and the 33 rails and the 178 braces. Fasten it with glue, the same glue on the Buy list. Where: The tip stands plumb, 15/16" tall. The 8 slanted tips run from 17 1/4" up to 23 1/16" up — end to end on the joints in the picture.||Every part on the bench is in a step.
Check plumb and square||Stand it up. Sight the long edges. If something racks, find the soft joint and re-join.||A lean now is a lean forever.

rows.steps:
Read this Brooklyn Bridge before you glue||802 full Standard Popsicle Sticks. Glue. Use it whole, as bought. Envelope about 139" × 12" × 6".||Trust the stick list — full pieces, no cuts.
Lay out the footprint on the bench||Tape a rectangle 138 1/2" × 6" on the bench. Mark centerlines both ways.||A square base keeps every later part true.
Raise the verticals — 56 legs||56 legs. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. Dry-fit the joint, then join. Verticals define the bays. Set the 56 legs on the floor, square to the marks. It is the base the next parts fasten to. Where: The 56 legs stand plumb, 4 1/2" tall.||Verticals define the bays.
Glue in the zigzag diagonals — 303 braces||303 braces. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. Dry-fit the joint, then join. Zigzag diagonals are the truss. Set the 303 braces on the floor, square to the marks. It is the base the next parts fasten to. Where: The braces lie at 2 1/2", 5 1/16" and 6 1/16" up from the bench (center lines). The 60 braces stand plumb, 4 1/2" tall. The 164 slanted braces run from 5 1/16" up to 11" up — end to end on the joints in the picture.||Zigzag diagonals are the truss.
Close the top chords and deck rails — 174 rails||174 rails. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. Dry-fit the joint, then join. Top chords finish the truss. Set the 174 rails on the 56 legs and the 303 braces. Fasten it with glue, the same glue on the Buy list. Where: The rails lie at 2 1/2", 5 1/16", 5 5/8", 5 5/8", 10 11/16" and 11" up from the bench (center lines). The 54 slanted rails run from 5 1/16" up to 11" up — end to end on the joints in the picture.||Top chords finish the truss.
Lay the road deck — cross-ties, then runners — 135 road members||135 road members. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. Dry-fit the joint, then join. The road you walk: same stock as the truss, on the deck rails. Where: All 135 decks lie 5 1/16" up from the bench (center line) — level with the tops of the legs.||The road you walk: same stock as the truss, on the deck rails.
Set the bottom chords — 134 supports||134 supports. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. Dry-fit the joint, then join. Lower chords carry the span. Set the 134 supports on the 56 legs and the 174 rails and the 135 decks and the 303 braces. Fasten it with glue, the same glue on the Buy list. Where: All 8 supports lie 5 1/16" up from the bench (center line) — level with the tops of the legs. The 126 slanted supports run from 5 1/16" up to 11" up — end to end on the joints in the picture.||Lower chords carry the span.
Check plumb and square||Stand it up. Sight the long edges. If something racks, find the soft joint and re-join.||A lean now is a lean forever.

rows.steps:
Read this Eiffel Tower before you glue||446 full Standard Popsicle Sticks. Glue. Use it whole, as bought. About 25" tall. Four arches, four piers, then one shaft — same tower as the bench. Each step lights only that part.||If a plate looks like a scribble, you are on the face lattice. Go back to the arches — those are the holes you walk through.
Tape the four feet on the bench||Tape a square 10 5/16" × 10 5/16". One pad per corner. Check both diagonals. Where: All 28 rings lie flat on the bench (center line).||A parallelogram base makes a leaning tower. Square it now, while it is easy to fix.
Glue the four arches||24 sticks — about 6 per arch. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. One chain of sticks per face. These are the four holes you walk through — the thing that makes it Eiffel, not a pyramid. Set the 24 supports on the floor, square to the marks. It is the base the next parts fasten to. Where: The 24 slanted supports run from the bench to 3 5/16" up — end to end on the joints in the picture.||One chain of sticks per face. These are the four holes you walk through — the thing that makes it Eiffel, not a pyramid.
Stand the four piers||56 sticks. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. Each corner is a thick lattice column up to the first deck. Where: The 56 slanted legs run from the bench to 4 1/4" up — end to end on the joints in the picture.||Each corner is a thick lattice column up to the first deck.
Close the first deck||44 sticks. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. This ring is the break in the picture: four legs become one shaft. Square it before you go up. Where: The rails lie at 4 1/4" and 5 5/8" up from the bench (center lines).||This ring is the break in the picture: four legs become one shaft. Square it before you go up.
Raise the shaft||48 sticks. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. Above the first deck the four piers have merged. Keep going up the center. Where: The 8 legs stand plumb, 1 9/16" tall. The 40 slanted legs run from 4 1/4" up to 22 1/4" up — end to end on the joints in the picture.||Above the first deck the four piers have merged. Keep going up the center.
Add the belts||40 sticks. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. Horizontal rings at the upper platforms. Where: The rails lie at 8 1/2", 11 5/8", 13 3/16", 14 9/16", 17 1/4" and 20 7/16" up from the bench (center lines).||Horizontal rings at the upper platforms.
Lace the face lattice||160 sticks. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. This is the texture in the render — the zigzag bracing on each face and between the piers. Set the 160 braces on the 128 rails and the 106 legs and the 24 supports. Fasten it with glue, the same glue on the Buy list. Where: The braces lie at 1 7/16", 2 13/16", 4 1/4", 5 5/8", 7 1/16" and 8 1/2" up from the bench (center lines). The 136 slanted braces run from 3 5/16" up to 22 1/4" up — end to end on the joints in the picture.||This is the texture in the render — the zigzag bracing on each face and between the piers.
Cap the lantern||2 sticks. Wood glue. Hold 30–60 seconds. Wipe squeeze-out. Let it cure overnight before it carries weight. The little cage at the tip. Where: The 2 slanted legs run from 22 1/4" up to 24 3/4" up — end to end on the joints in the picture.||The little cage at the tip.
Stand it up and walk around||If an arch sags, that joint was dry. Overnight before you lift by the tip.||Guidance only — not stamped engineering.
